docs.title: zer0sh Dotfiles
docs.text:
Welcome to the official documentation for zer0sh's desktop environment, built on Hyprland (Wayland) and customized with Quickshell, Waybar, Kitty / Alacritty, and Zsh.

Quick Install View Repository

docs.title: Design Philosophy
docs.text:
• Strict Modularity

    No monolithic configuration files. Every concern (keybindings, monitor layouts, animations, autostart services) is isolated into its own dedicated file.

  • Direct Live Source of Truth

    The live Hyprland configuration resides directly in ~/.config/hypr/ as a real, independent directory, allowing seamless live edits without symlink friction.

  • Cohesive Visual Integration

    Centralized palettes generated across Quickshell, Hyprland borders, Waybar, and terminal emulators.

  • Fluid Modern OSDs & Notifications

    Floating surfaces anchored at the top-center of the screen, featuring smooth downward slide-in transitions and fluid stack displacement.

docs.title: Bat Syntax Pager & Cat Clone
docs.text: bat is a modern replacement for the traditional Unix cat command, enhanced with syntax highlighting for hundreds of programming and markup languages, Git modification badges, automatic terminal detection, and customizable paging styles.

docs.title: File Structure & Paths
docs.text:
• Repository configuration: ~/dotfiles/bat/config
  • Target symlink: ~/.config/bat/config -> ~/dotfiles/bat/config
  • Debian binary: /usr/bin/batcat
  • Local symlink: ~/.local/bin/bat -> /usr/bin/batcat
  • Shell alias: alias cat='batcat' (configured in ~/dotfiles/zsh/zshrc_aliases)

docs.title: Configuration (config)
docs.text:
The active configuration resides in ~/.config/bat/config:

--style=header
--color=always
--wrap=never
--paging=never
--tabs=4

docs.title: Parameter Breakdown
docs.text:
• --style=header: Displays a compact header containing the file path and file type metadata above the file contents, omitting line number grids to keep terminal output clean and easily selectable for copying.
  • --color=always: Guarantees syntax highlighting is rendered even when piping or redirecting stdout where color tags are accepted.
  • --wrap=never: Prevents long lines of code from auto-wrapping across multiple visual rows, maintaining formatting integrity.
  • --paging=never: Emulates traditional cat by streaming output directly to the terminal stdout without piping into a pager like less. This eliminates extra keypresses (q) when viewing short files or running shell scripts.
  • --tabs=4: Standardizes tab stop indentation to 4 characters.

docs.title: Debian Packaging & Binary Resolution
docs.text:
On Debian and Ubuntu systems, the executable binary is packaged as batcat by the package manager (apt install bat) to prevent naming collisions with a legacy Debian package.

To provide a seamless workflow across different distributions and tools:

  1. Local Symlink: The dotfiles deployment script creates a symlink in ~/.local/bin/bat pointing to /usr/bin/batcat.
  2. Shell Alias: alias cat='batcat' in ~/.zshrc_aliases replaces default cat calls transparently.
  3. Plain Cat Fallback: When pure unformatted POSIX cat behavior is required, invoke \cat or /bin/cat.

docs.title: Common Commands & Usage Patterns
docs.text:
# View file with syntax highlighting and file header
cat file.py
bat file.py

# View with full line numbers and git modifications grid
bat --style=full file.py

# Highlight piped input explicitly specifying language
curl -s https://api.github.com | bat -l json

# Inspect Git diff modifications directly in the file
bat --diff file.rs

# List available syntax highlighting themes
bat --list-themes

docs.title: btop Resource Monitor
docs.text: btop is a GPU/CPU/Memory/Disk/Network terminal resource monitor whose dashboard colors are regenerated from the active wallpaper by Matugen.

docs.title: File Structure & Paths
docs.text:
• Repository configuration: ~/dotfiles/btop/btop.conf
  • Local configuration symlink: ~/.config/btop/btop.conf -> ~/dotfiles/btop/btop.conf
  • Custom themes directory: ~/.config/btop/themes/
  • Active dynamic theme symlink: ~/.config/btop/themes/matugen.theme -> ~/.config/themes/current/btop.theme
  • Automation setup script: ~/dotfiles/scripts/setup-btop-matugen.sh

docs.title: Dynamic Matugen Integration
docs.text:
btop inherits the active desktop color palette generated by Matugen from the current wallpaper:

Wallpaper Image (.png / .jpg)
          |
          v
   [ matugen image ]
          |
          v (evaluates ~/.config/matugen/templates/btop.theme)
~/.config/themes/current/btop.theme
          |
          v (symlink)
~/.config/btop/themes/matugen.theme
          |
          v (consumed by)
btop (color_theme = "/home/zero/.config/btop/themes/matugen.theme", theme_background = True)

docs.title: Key Theme Settings in btop.conf
docs.text:
• color_theme = "/home/zero/.config/btop/themes/matugen.theme": Absolute path to the theme symlink, which resolves to the freshly generated ~/.config/themes/current/btop.theme on every wallpaper change.
  • theme_background = True: btop is allowed to paint its own dashboard background. The Matugen template emits an empty main_bg, so no background color is forced and the terminal background from Alacritty stays visible. Set it to False to make btop always defer to the terminal background.
  • truecolor = True: Enables full 24-bit RGB color depth.

docs.title: Automated Theme Deployment
docs.text:
To initialize or refresh the btop dynamic theme, run:

~/dotfiles/scripts/setup-btop-matugen.sh

Whenever wallpapers are changed via the Quickshell Control Center, ~/.config/themes/apply-matugen.sh automatically re-renders btop.theme alongside all other desktop components.

docs.title: Key Settings & Presets
docs.text:
• Update rate: 2000ms (update_ms = 2000).
  • Process sorting: Sorted by CPU usage in descending order (proc_sorting = "cpu lazy", proc_reversed = True).
  • Presets: Quick layout profiles configured via presets in btop.conf (switchable using keys 1 through 9).

docs.title: Fastfetch Configuration
docs.text: Fastfetch is a lightweight, ultra-fast system information tool configured to display system hardware, environment telemetry, and desktop branding across Alacritty and other terminal sessions.

docs.title: File Structure & Paths
docs.text:

  • Custom logo art: ~/dotfiles/fastfetch/logo.txt
  • Target symlink: ~/.config/fastfetch -> ~/dotfiles/fastfetch

docs.title: Layout & Visual Architecture
docs.text: The configuration leverages custom braille ASCII art alongside structured telemetry modules styled with the system's red primary accent:

docs.title: 1. Logo Section
docs.text:
• Type: File-based logo sourced from ~/.config/fastfetch/logo.txt.
  • Art style: High-density Unicode/Braille graphic emblem.
  • Color: Pure red ("1": "red").
  • Spacing: 4 characters of right-side padding to separate art from text keys.

docs.title: 2. Display and Bar Formatting
docs.text:
• Separator: Custom arrow delimiter colored red.
  • Progress Bars: Dual-line glyph bars (━ elapsed, ─ remaining) enclosed in bracket borders [ ] for graphical representation of:
  • System Memory (RAM) utilization.
  • Root disk partition capacity (used / total (percentage)).
  • Battery charge level and AC power status.

docs.title: 3. Displayed Modules
docs.text:
• User & Host: user@host with custom color formatting.
  • Operating System: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (Trixie) x86_64.
  • Kernel: Active Linux kernel build and architecture.
  • Uptime: Session elapsed time.
  • Packages: Total dpkg package count.
  • Shell: Current interactive shell binary (Zsh Shell Configuration).
  • Window Manager: Hyprland Compositor Architecture version and protocol.
  • Hardware: CPU model and maximum frequency, integrated GPU chipset.
  • Memory & Storage: Real-time RAM and storage consumption.
  • Battery: Charge percentage and charging status.
  • Terminal Palette: 8 circular color swatches positioned at the base, reflecting the active Matugen Color Palette.

docs.text:

fastfetch

Fastfetch can also be hooked into your interactive shell greeting inside .zshrc (see Zsh Configuration).

docs.title: Matugen Dynamic Theming Engine
docs.text: Matugen is the Material You (Material Design 3) color palette generator used in this desktop environment. It extracts harmonic color palettes from wallpaper images and propagates them to all active UI components through dynamic templates.

docs.title: Architectural Role and Store
docs.text:
• Engine Configuration: ~/.config/matugen/config.toml (version-controlled in ~/dotfiles/matugen/config.toml).
  • Template Repository: ~/.config/matugen/templates/ contains component-specific template files.
  • Central Theme Store: Output files are rendered directly into ~/.config/themes/current/, which acts as the single source of truth for the entire desktop.
Wallpaper Image (.png / .jpg)
          |
          v
   [ matugen image ]
          |
          v  (processes ~/.config/matugen/templates/)
~/.config/themes/current/
   ├── alacritty.toml  --> read by ~/.config/alacritty/alacritty.toml
   ├── wofi.css        --> imported by ~/.config/wofi/style.css
   ├── waybar.css      --> imported by ~/.config/waybar/colors.css
   ├── kitty.conf      --> included by ~/.config/kitty/kitty.conf
   ├── hyprland.conf   --> sourced by Hyprland for active/inactive borders
   ├── hyprlock.conf   --> sourced by ~/.config/hypr/hyprlock.conf
   ├── hyprtoolkit.conf --> read by hyprpolkitagent and Hyprland/QML apps (rendered to ~/.config/hypr/)
   ├── btop.theme       --> linked by ~/.config/btop/themes/matugen.theme
   ├── gtk-3.0.css     --> linked by ~/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css
   ├── gtk-4.0.css     --> linked by ~/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css
   ├── spicetify.ini   --> linked by ~/.config/spicetify/Themes/matugen/color.ini
   ├── steam.css       --> linked by ~/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam/custom/custom.css
   ├── palette.json    --> consumed by Quickshell Control Center & Widgets
   ├── matugen.vim     --> loaded by Vim via :colorscheme matugen
   └── vscode-colors / vscode-colors.json --> watched by the VS Code "Matugen Theme" extension (rendered to ~/.cache/matugen/)
    └── zen-userchrome.css / zen-usercontent.css --> rendered into <profile>/chrome/ and imported by userChrome.css / userContent.css

Note: the outputs rendered outside ~/.config/themes/current/ are the exceptions to the central store. hyprtoolkit.conf goes to ~/.config/hypr/hyprtoolkit.conf, the VS Code outputs go to ~/.cache/matugen/vscode-colors and ~/.cache/matugen/vscode-colors.json because the haikalllp.matugen-theme extension watches those hardcoded paths, and the Zen Browser outputs go to the profile chrome/ folder because Firefox forks only load stylesheets from the profile.

# Matugen is the color generator; ~/.config/themes is the central theme store.

type = "scheme-vibrant"
source_color_index = 0

[templates.waybar]
input_path = "~/.config/matugen/templates/waybar.css"
output_path = "~/.config/themes/current/waybar.css"

docs.title: Themed GTK Applications Suite
docs.text:
The generated stylesheets dynamically theme classic and modern GTK applications to match the active desktop palette, inspired by Mitsugen:

  • Ultra-Clean Headerbars: Window controls (minimize, maximize, close buttons) are hidden via gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.wm.preferences button-layout ":" and GTK CSS, keeping titlebars distraction-free.
  • Unified Surface: Headerbars blend seamlessly with @window_bg_color, allowing sidebars and view panes to extend smoothly from top to bottom without harsh division borders.
  • Refined Navigation & Breadcrumbs: Nautilus navigation sidebars use soft rounded pills with accent translucency (alpha(@accent_bg_color, 0.18)), and pathbar breadcrumbs adopt rounded corners.
  • Modern GTK3 Foundation: GTK3 applications consume the custom-dark / custom-light base themes (adw-gtk3), unifying classic and modern apps under a single Libadwaita design language.

docs.title: Papirus Folders Dynamic Theming
docs.text: Papirus icon folders automatically adapt to the desktop wallpaper without requiring root privileges or sudoers modifications:

docs.title: 1. The Name Collision Problem & User Namespace Solution
docs.text:
In modern Wayland and GTK 4 setups (such as Nautilus in GNOME 48), if an icon theme named Papirus-Dark exists in both /usr/share/icons/ and ~/.local/share/icons/, GTK 4 resolves system paths first, falling back to unmodifiable blue folders.

To overcome this without requiring sudo on every wallpaper switch, the environment provisions dedicated user-space themes in ~/.local/share/icons/: * Papirus-Matugen-Dark (inherits Papirus-Dark,Papirus,breeze-dark,hicolor) * Papirus-Matugen-Light (inherits Papirus-Light,Papirus,breeze,hicolor)

Because these theme names do not exist in /usr/share/icons/, GTK 4 is guaranteed to load the user's local instance.

docs.title: 2. Helper Scripts Required
docs.text:
Two scripts manage this pipeline inside ~/dotfiles/scripts/:

  • scripts/papirus-folders: The official Papirus folder recoloring script bundled directly in the dotfiles repository and deployed to ~/.local/bin/papirus-folders.
  • scripts/setup-papirus-matugen.sh: One-time setup utility (executed automatically by install.sh) that:
  • Installs the papirus-folders binary to ~/.local/bin/.
  • Copies system Papirus themes to ~/.local/share/icons/Papirus-Matugen-Dark and Papirus-Matugen-Light.
  • Rewrites their index.theme to update Name and configure Inherits fallback to the system package.
  • Generates an initial icon cache via gtk-update-icon-cache.

To manually trigger or reinitialize the user icon themes: 

~/dotfiles/scripts/setup-papirus-matugen.sh

    { name = "yellow",     color = "#f9bd30" },
]
compare_to = "{{ colors.primary.default.hex }}"
post_hook = "sh -c '(papirus-folders -t Papirus-Matugen-Dark -C {{ closest_color }} && papirus-folders -t Papirus-Matugen-Light -C {{ closest_color }} && papirus-folders -t Papirus-Matugen -C {{ closest_color }}) >/dev/null 2>&1 &'"
index = 1

The template file matugen/templates/papirus-color simply stores: 

current={{colors.primary.default.hex_stripped}}

docs.title: 4. Live Reloading in apply-matugen.sh
docs.text: Whenever apply-matugen.sh runs: 1. It writes gtk-icon-theme-name=Papirus-Matugen-Dark (or Papirus-Matugen-Light) into both ~/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini and ~/.config/gtk-4.0/settings.ini. 2. Updates gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface icon-theme. 3. Runs Matugen, which switches the symlinks in ~/.local/share/icons/Papirus-Matugen-Dark/ to the nearest matching color. 4. Toggles icon-theme to Adwaita and back to force running GTK 4 apps (such as Nautilus) to immediately invalidate their icon cache without needing a session restart.

docs.title: Material Bibata Dynamic Cursor Theming
docs.text: The mouse cursor dynamically re-tones itself on every wallpaper switch to harmoniously match the Material Design 3 primary accent, integrating Material Bibata Cursor created by Sakib Shahariar:

docs.title: 1. Perceptual Palette Matching (CIEDE2000)
docs.text:
Rather than converting colors through distorted HSV color spaces, the system calculates perceptual distance using the CIEDE2000 Delta-E algorithm in CIELAB space via themes/color_match.py. It compares the active wallpaper's primary hex token against 28 curated M3 tonal pairs in themes/bibata-themes.json (plus Classic).

  • Dark Mode: Activates the dark container body with saturated tonal border (e.g., Bibata-Material-Lime, Bibata-Material-Teal).
  • Light Mode: Automatically routes to the matching tone-swapped variant with -Light suffix (e.g., Bibata-Material-Lime-Light), preserving high contrast standards (>= 4.5:1).

docs.title: 2. Cross-Desktop Application Sync
docs.text: When themes/apply-matugen.sh runs: 1. Resolves the optimal cursor theme name via python3 themes/color_match.py <primary_hex> themes/bibata-themes.json. 2. Persists the active theme name to ~/.config/themes/current/cursor-theme. 3. Dispatches live cursor updates to Hyprland (hyprctl setcursor <theme> 24). 4. Updates GNOME / GTK settings via gsettings set org.gnome.desktop.interface cursor-theme <theme>. 5. Updates GTK configuration files (~/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini and ~/.config/gtk-4.0/settings.ini). 6. Overwrites ~/.icons/default/index.theme for legacy X11 / XCursor applications.

docs.title: 3. Setup and Deployment
docs.text:
The setup utility scripts/setup-bibata-matugen.sh deploys the official pre-built v1.5.0 assets directly to ~/.local/share/icons/ with symlinks in ~/.icons/, verified during initial ./install.sh.

~/dotfiles/scripts/setup-bibata-matugen.sh

docs.title: Core Color Roles
docs.text:
Each template uses standardized Material Design 3 tokens:

  • colors.background.default.hex: Deep primary canvas background.
  • colors.surface.default.hex: Floating surface and card backdrop.
  • colors.surface_container.default.hex: Inactive inputs and container elements.
  • colors.surface_bright.default.hex: Subtle highlight outlines and borders.
  • colors.primary.default.hex: Main accent color, active borders, and focus rings.
  • colors.primary_container.default.hex: Low-contrast selection backgrounds.
  • colors.on_surface.default.hex: Primary text and foreground iconography.
  • colors.on_surface_variant.default.hex: Secondary text, metadata, and hints.
  • colors.outline.default.hex: Structural dividers and borders.
  • colors.error.default.hex: Destructive actions and critical warnings.
  • colors.tertiary.default.hex: Auxiliary highlights, charging states, and indicators.

docs.title: CLI Usage and Manual Palette Generation
docs.text:
To generate a new palette from any wallpaper image:

# Preview extracted palette without writing files
matugen image "/path/to/wallpaper.jpg" --mode dark --dry-run --show-colors

# Generate palette and update all theme templates
matugen image "/path/to/wallpaper.jpg" --mode dark --source-color-index 0

Optionally adjust the contrast level using --contrast: 

# Increase contrast for accessibility or higher distinction (-1.0 to 1.0)
matugen image "/path/to/wallpaper.jpg" --mode dark --contrast 0.2

docs.title: Orchestration: apply-matugen.sh
docs.text:
~/dotfiles/themes/apply-matugen.sh is the single entrypoint that regenerates the whole palette. It is invoked by Quickshell when the wallpaper changes (modules/background/Background.qml), by the theme picker in the Control Center (modules/controlcenter/ControlCenter.qml), and manually from a shell.

Inputs, in order of precedence: the optional first argument, then the ~/.config/themes/current/wallpaper state file. The mode (dark/light) follows the optional second argument, then ~/.config/themes/current/mode, defaulting to dark. The color scheme type (scheme-vibrant, scheme-fruit-salad, scheme-monochrome, etc.) follows the optional third argument, then ~/.config/themes/current/scheme_type, defaulting to scheme-vibrant. All three state files are rewritten on every run.

The script executes:

  1. matugen image with --config ~/.config/matugen/config.toml, -t "$TYPE", --contrast 0.2, --mode "$MODE", --source-color-index 0 and --quiet (the index flag bypasses the interactive color picker).
  2. hyprctl reload to re-read the generated border colors.
  3. pkill -SIGUSR2 waybar to reload the status bar stylesheet.
  4. Writes matugen to ~/.config/quickshell/current-theme so Quickshell consumes palette.json instead of a static theme.
  5. Sets org.gnome.desktop.interface color-scheme to prefer-dark or prefer-light, sets icon-theme (Papirus-Dark or Papirus-Light), enforces button-layout ":" to hide window controls, and toggles gtk-theme to force GTK stylesheets to re-read with custom-dark or custom-light.
  6. Spawns spicetify apply -n in the background (&) only when the active Spicetify theme is matugen.
  7. Runs ~/.config/themes/update-wallpaper-cache.sh to refresh wallpaper thumbnails.

No reload step is needed for Alacritty (automatic live reload), for VS Code (the extension watches ~/.cache/matugen/), or for the root symlinks created by sync-root-theme.sh (they point at themes/current/). Zen Browser cannot be reloaded programmatically either: the rendered zen-userChrome.css and zen-userContent.css are picked up on the next full browser restart. Steam is re-injected automatically by its post_hook on every render, but the client must be restarted to display the refreshed palette. Similarly, Spicetify permanently injects the updated matugen palette into Spotify via spicetify apply -n; if a Spotify window is currently active in Hyprland, the background worker automatically dispatches a native Ctrl + Shift + R reload shortcut via hyprctl dispatch sendshortcut to reload the interface live with the new colors without closing the client or stopping music playback. Because Spotify runs through XWayland to bypass CEF Wayland GPU crashes, context menu blur and shadow artifacts are eliminated using specialized compositor rules (see XWayland & Window Rules).

docs.title: Privileged Applications Theming (sudo / root)
docs.text:
By default, applications executed with sudo (such as administrative tools, file managers, or system monitors) read configuration files from /root/.config/ and do not inherit user-level CSS overrides.

To synchronize your active Matugen theme with the root user:

sudo ~/dotfiles/scripts/sync-root-theme.sh

docs.title: Mechanism and Persistence:
docs.text:
1. Creates /root/.config/gtk-3.0/ and /root/.config/gtk-4.0/.
  2. Configures Adwaita-dark preference in /root/.config/gtk-3.0/settings.ini.
  3. Symlinks root GTK stylesheets directly to the user's central theme store:
  4. /root/.config/gtk-3.0/gtk.css -> ~/.config/themes/current/gtk-3.0.css
  5. /root/.config/gtk-4.0/gtk.css -> ~/.config/themes/current/gtk-4.0.css
  6. Symlinks root btop monitor theme (/root/.config/btop/themes/matugen.theme).

Because these are live symlinks targeting ~/.config/themes/current/, subsequent wallpaper or palette changes made via Quickshell will automatically reflect in root applications without re-executing the synchronization script.

docs.title: Synchronization & Cleanup Flags
docs.text:
The sync-root-theme.sh utility provides flags to manage synchronization or easily restore default themes:

Flag Privilege Description --sync (default) sudo Synchronize root GTK and btop themes from active user theme. --cleanup-user User Revert user GTK3 and GTK4 stylesheets to system defaults. --cleanup-root sudo Remove root theme symlinks and restore original settings. --cleanup-all sudo Revert both user and root configurations to factory defaults. 
# Revert user theme only (no sudo required)
~/dotfiles/scripts/sync-root-theme.sh --cleanup-user

# Revert root theme only
sudo ~/dotfiles/scripts/sync-root-theme.sh --cleanup-root

# Revert both user and root to system defaults
sudo ~/dotfiles/scripts/sync-root-theme.sh --cleanup-all

docs.title: Manual Installation: VS Code Theme Integration (Pilot)
docs.text:
Standalone instructions to add the VS Code theme integration to an existing matugen installation without cloning the full dotfiles repository. This is the pilot for the manual installation format used across this documentation.

All snippets are compatible with bash and zsh, use explicit paths only (no glob patterns), and are safe to paste into an interactive shell.

docs.title: Files created or modified
docs.text: Action Path Notes Create ~/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors Raw color list template Create ~/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors.json JSON color template Modify (backup first) ~/.config/matugen/config.toml Registers both templates Create ~/.cache/matugen/vscode-colors Rendered by matugen Create ~/.cache/matugen/vscode-colors.json Rendered by matugen

docs.title: Step 1: Validate prerequisites
docs.text:
Run the checks. Every line must report OK before continuing, except extension: a missing extension here is expected, because Step 6 installs it:

command -v matugen >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "matugen       : OK" || echo "matugen       : MISSING"
command -v code >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "vscode cli    : OK" || echo "vscode cli    : MISSING"
command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "curl          : OK" || echo "curl          : MISSING"
test -d "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates" && echo "templates dir : OK" || echo "templates dir : MISSING"
test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" && echo "config.toml   : OK" || echo "config.toml   : MISSING"
code --list-extensions 2>/dev/null | grep -Fx "haikalllp.matugen-theme" >/dev/null && echo "extension     : OK" || echo "extension     : MISSING"

If a line reports MISSING:

  • matugen: install it from https://github.com/InioX/matugen.
  • vscode cli: install VS Code and make sure the code command is in PATH.
  • curl: install it with your package manager (apt install curl on Debian).
  • templates dir: create it with mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates".
  • config.toml: create an empty one with touch "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml".
  • extension: the haikalllp.matugen-theme theme extension is not installed yet; Step 6 installs it, so no action is needed here.

docs.title: Step 2: Back up the files that will be modified
docs.text:
The only existing file altered by this procedure is config.toml. The backup name carries the exact date and time of the operation:

BACKUP_STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
cp -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"
echo "Backup created: $HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"

If template files from a previous attempt already exist, they are backed up the same way before being replaced:

BACKUP_STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
if test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors"; then
    cp -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors" "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"
fi
if test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors.json"; then
    cp -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors.json" "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors.json.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"
fi

docs.title: Step 3: Create the template files
docs.text:
Download both templates directly from the repository:

mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates"
curl -fsSL -o "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors" "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zer0sh/dotfiles/main/matugen/templates/vscode-colors"
curl -fsSL -o "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors.json" "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zer0sh/dotfiles/main/matugen/templates/vscode-colors.json"

Alternatively, copy the file contents manually from the repository pages (vscode-colors, vscode-colors.json) into the destination paths shown above.

Confirm both files exist and are not empty:

test -s "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors" && echo "vscode-colors      : OK" || echo "vscode-colors      : MISSING"
test -s "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors.json" && echo "vscode-colors.json : OK" || echo "vscode-colors.json : MISSING"

docs.title: Step 4: Register the templates in config.toml
docs.text:
The following block is idempotent: it appends the sections only when they are not already registered. The heredoc delimiter is quoted, so no variable or shell expansion happens inside it:

if grep -q "^\[templates.vscode-raw\]" "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml"; then
    echo "Already registered in config.toml, nothing to do."
else
    cat >> "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" <<'EOF'

# VS Code (haikalllp.matugen-theme extension watches these paths)
[templates.vscode-raw]
input_path = "~/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors"
output_path = "~/.cache/matugen/vscode-colors"

[templates.vscode-json]
input_path = "~/.config/matugen/templates/vscode-colors.json"
output_path = "~/.cache/matugen/vscode-colors.json"
EOF
    echo "Registered in config.toml."
fi

docs.title: Step 5: Generate the colors
docs.text:
Replace the wallpaper path with your own absolute path. The --source-color-index 0 flag disables the interactive color picker, so the command also works from keybindings or non-interactive shells:

matugen image "/absolute/path/to/your-wallpaper.jpg" --mode dark --source-color-index 0
test -f "$HOME/.cache/matugen/vscode-colors" && echo "rendered colors : OK" || echo "rendered colors : MISSING"

docs.title: Step 6: Install the extension and activate the theme
docs.text:
code --install-extension haikalllp.matugen-theme

Then in VS Code press Ctrl+K Ctrl+T and select Matugen (or Matugen Bordered for panels with border lines).

docs.title: Step 7: Verification
docs.text:
test -f "$HOME/.cache/matugen/vscode-colors" && echo "colors      : OK" || echo "colors      : MISSING"
code --list-extensions | grep -Fx "haikalllp.matugen-theme" >/dev/null && echo "extension   : OK" || echo "extension   : MISSING"
find "$HOME/.vscode/extensions" -maxdepth 2 -type f -name "matugen.json" -path "*matugen-theme*" 2>/dev/null | grep -q . && echo "theme file  : OK" || echo "theme file  : MISSING"

Note: the -name and -path values in the find command are find predicates, not shell patterns, so they are never expanded by the shell.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• themes/matugen.json does not exist or VS Code reports it cannot load the theme: the extension activated before the color files were generated, so its file watcher missed them. Open the Command Palette and run Matugen Theme: Update Theme, or reload the window with Developer: Reload Window.
  • Palette did not change after a wallpaper switch: run matugen image again (Step 5) and check the Output panel of VS Code, channel Matugen Theme.
  • Restore the previous configuration: copy the backup created in Step 2 back over config.toml using the exact name printed by the backup command.

docs.title: Caso Particular: Latencia en Transición y Ventanas Desincronizadas
1. Síntomas Reportados
docs.text:
• Sensación de bloqueo y estancamiento: Al alternar esquemas de Matugen o temas manuales desde Quickshell, el escritorio no respondía de inmediato (demoras perceptibles de entre 10 y 15 segundos). Durante este periodo, selecciones subsecuentes quedaban descartadas o ignoradas.
  • Ventanas desfasadas en el tema anterior: Varias ventanas (como aplicaciones GTK4/Libadwaita, navegadores o terminales) mantenían los colores del tema previo incluso tras cerrarlas y abrirlas nuevamente.

docs.title: 2. Diagnóstico y Análisis de Causa Raíz
A. Bloqueos Síncronos Masivos de E/S (14s en Matugen)
docs.text:
• Papirus Folders (matugen/config.toml): El post_hook de Matugen para Papirus ejecutaba de manera síncrona papirus-folders en tres colecciones completas (Papirus-Matugen-Dark, Papirus-Matugen-Light y Papirus-Matugen). Cada invocación inspecciona y reescribe miles de enlaces simbólicos SVG en disco. Tiempo medido: ~8.43 segundos.
  • Spicetify (apply-matugen.sh): Al finalizar la generación, se ejecutaba spicetify apply -n bloqueando la finalización del script. Tiempo medido: ~3.97 segundos.
  • Impacto en Quickshell (QProcess): Quickshell despacha los comandos de cambio de tema a través de componentes Process { id: ... }. En la arquitectura de Quickshell/Qt, si una orden se dispara mientras running === true, reasignar command y forzar running = true no reinicia ni encola el proceso. Cualquier clic posterior durante esos 14 segundos resultaba ignorado.

docs.title: B. Timeout de Socket Terminal (10s en apply-theme.sh)
docs.text: • Llamada a Kitty sin socket IPC: En quickshell/scripts/apply-theme.sh, se ejecutaba kitty @ set-colors --all --configured "$KITTY_COLORS_FILE". Al no estar Kitty configurado con un socket Unix (listen_on unix:...), el cliente IPC de Kitty aguardaba una conexión hasta agotar su tiempo límite interno. Tiempo medido: 10.03 segundos exactos (Error: i/o timeout). Hasta no agotarse ese timeout, los bordes de Hyprland (hyprctl keyword) no se aplicaban.

docs.title: C. Asimetría de Hojas de Estilo GTK
docs.text: • Mientras apply-matugen.sh generaba gtk-3.0.css y gtk-4.0.css en ~/.config/themes/current/, el script de temas manuales (apply-theme.sh) omitía por completo estas plantillas. Cuando el usuario seleccionaba un tema manual (md3-crimson-night, cyberpunk, custom), las aplicaciones GTK (como Shortwave o Nautilus) continuaban leyendo el último archivo CSS generado por Matugen.

docs.title: D. Ciclo de Vida de Procesos y Daemons
docs.text:
• Zen Browser (Firefox Gecko): Zen no lee userChrome.css en caliente ni al abrir pestañas/ventanas adicionales si el proceso principal (/app/zen/zen-bin) permanece en ejecución en segundo plano. Cerrar una ventana individual no recrea el runtime de estilos; se requiere un cierre total (Ctrl + Q o terminar el proceso).
  • Steam: El botón cerrar ventana minimiza la aplicación a la bandeja del sistema (System Tray); el cliente continúa en memoria con los recursos cargados.
  • Kitty: Kitty no implementa recarga de configuración bajo SIGUSR1. Las ventanas existentes conservan sus colores a menos que se use el atajo interno (Ctrl + Shift + F5), mientras que las ventanas nuevas sí leen el nuevo kitty.conf.

docs.title: 3. Soluciones Arquitectónicas Implementadas
docs.text: Componente Estado Anterior Solución Aplicada Impacto matugen/config.toml (Papirus) Hook síncrono ejecutando 3 comandos secuenciales Desacople a subshell asíncrono en segundo plano: sh -c '(papirus-folders ...) >/dev/null 2>&1 &' De 8.5s a 0.002s en el hilo principal apply-matugen.sh (Spicetify) Ejecución síncrona en primer plano Ejecución en background: (spicetify apply -n && sendshortcut) & De 4.0s a 0s de bloqueo apply-theme.sh (Kitty IPC) kitty @ set-colors bloqueante con timeout Eliminación de la llamada con timeout; Alacritty recarga live y nuevas ventanas de Kitty leen kitty.conf De 10.03s a 0.11s de tiempo total apply-theme.sh (GTK 3 & 4) Sin generación de estilos GTK Síntesis directa de tokens MD3 en gtk-3.0.css y gtk-4.0.css con notificación vía gsettings Paridad completa entre temas manuales y dinámicos

docs.title: 4. Benchmarks de Rendimiento
docs.text:
Transición Matugen (apply-matugen.sh):
  Antes : 14.107s (bloqueado en disco y asset patch)
  Después:  0.718s (20x más rápido, respuesta interactiva instantánea)

Transición Temas Manuales (apply-theme.sh):
  Antes : 10.120s (congelado por I/O timeout de Kitty)
  Después:  0.117s (90x más rápido)

docs.title: Steam Client Theming
docs.text:
The Steam desktop client is integrated into the dynamic Material You theming pipeline using Matugen templates and the native installer of Adwaita-for-Steam (Foldex fork, MIT). The pipeline extracts harmonic colors from the active desktop wallpaper and renders custom CSS variables that cover Steam's window surfaces, headerbars, popovers, sidebars, cards, and accent highlights.

The injection runs through install.py with Python 3 only. Flatpak and the AdwSteamGtk graphical wrapper are not required; they remain an optional alternative (see Optional: AdwSteamGtk Graphical Wrapper).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Requirement Minimum Purpose Validate with Steam (native) any Receives the patched stylesheets under ~/.local/share/Steam/steamui command -v steam Millennium (optional) 3.x Steam modding framework for companion skins and plugins; not required by this pipeline test -f /usr/lib/millennium/libmillennium_hhx64.so python3 3.9+ (system ships 3.13) Executes install.py python3 --version git any Clones Adwaita-for-Steam once command -v git matugen 4.x Renders the Material Design 3 palette from a wallpaper command -v matugen Matugen engine config any Provides ~/.config/matugen/config.toml and ~/.config/matugen/templates/ test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" bash or zsh any Runs the snippets of this guide echo $0

No sudo privileges are required. Every path touched by the integration lives under $HOME, and the Steam client directory is only modified inside the user-owned steamui folder.

docs.title: 1. Matugen Template (matugen/templates/steam.css)
docs.text:
The template defines Adwaita-compatible variables translated from Material Design 3 color tokens. The RGB triplets are comma-separated because Adwaita-for-Steam consumes them through legacy rgb(var(--name)) and rgba(var(--name), alpha) functions:

/*
* GTK 4 / Adwaita for Steam Colors
* Material You dynamic template generated by Matugen
*
* RGB triplets are comma-separated because Adwaita-for-Steam consumes them
* through legacy rgb(var(--name)) and rgba(var(--name), alpha) functions.
*/

:root {
    --adw-accent-rgb: {{ colors.primary.default.red }}, {{ colors.primary.default.green }}, {{ colors.primary.default.blue }};
    --adw-accent-bg-rgb: {{ colors.primary.default.red }}, {{ colors.primary.default.green }}, {{ colors.primary.default.blue }};
    --adw-accent-fg-rgb: {{ colors.on_primary.default.red }}, {{ colors.on_primary.default.green }}, {{ colors.on_primary.default.blue }};

    --adw-window-bg-rgb: {{ colors.background.default.red }}, {{ colors.background.default.green }}, {{ colors.background.default.blue }};
    --adw-window-fg-rgb: {{ colors.on_background.default.red }}, {{ colors.on_background.default.green }}, {{ colors.on_background.default.blue }};

    --adw-headerbar-bg-rgb: {{ colors.surface_dim.default.red }}, {{ colors.surface_dim.default.green }}, {{ colors.surface_dim.default.blue }};
    --adw-headerbar-fg-rgb: {{ colors.on_surface.default.red }}, {{ colors.on_surface.default.green }}, {{ colors.on_surface.default.blue }};

    --adw-popover-bg-rgb: {{ colors.surface_dim.default.red }}, {{ colors.surface_dim.default.green }}, {{ colors.surface_dim.default.blue }};
    --adw-popover-fg-rgb: {{ colors.on_surface.default.red }}, {{ colors.on_surface.default.green }}, {{ colors.on_surface.default.blue }};

    --adw-view-fg-rgb: {{ colors.on_surface.default.red }}, {{ colors.on_surface.default.green }}, {{ colors.on_surface.default.blue }};

    --adw-card-bg-rgb: {{ colors.surface.default.red }}, {{ colors.surface.default.green }}, {{ colors.surface.default.blue }};

    --adw-sidebar-fg-rgb: {{ colors.on_background.default.red }}, {{ colors.on_background.default.green }}, {{ colors.on_background.default.blue }};
    --adw-sidebar-border-rgb: {{ colors.background.default.red }}, {{ colors.background.default.green }}, {{ colors.background.default.blue }};
    --adw-sidebar-backdrop-rgb: {{ colors.background.default.red }}, {{ colors.background.default.green }}, {{ colors.background.default.blue }};
}

The variables are declared in :root, so every adwaita stylesheet (imported before custom/custom.css) resolves them against the current palette. Upstream defaults cover the variables the template does not override (destructive, warning, success and online/offline colors).

docs.title: 2. Matugen Mapping (matugen/config.toml)
docs.text:
The engine config renders the template into the central store and re-injects the theme:

[templates.steam]
input_path = "~/.config/matugen/templates/steam.css"
output_path = "~/.config/themes/current/steam.css"
post_hook = 'cd "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam" && python3 install.py --custom-css -t normal >/dev/null 2>&1 || true'

Hook behavior:

  • cd into the clone first, because install.py refuses to run outside its repository root.
  • --custom-css imports custom/custom.css (the symlink to themes/current/steam.css) as the last stylesheet, so the palette overrides every upstream default.
  • -t normal targets native Steam (~/.steam/steam); the flatpak target is never used.
  • Output is silenced and the command always succeeds (|| true), so a missing Steam installation or a missing clone can never break palette generation.

docs.title: Automatic Installation (Dotfiles)
docs.text:
Running ~/dotfiles/install.sh invokes the setup script when Steam is detected:

if command -v steam >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ -d "$HOME/.steam/steam" ]; then
    "$REPO_DIR/scripts/setup-steam-matugen.sh"
fi

The setup script is idempotent and can be re-run at any time:

~/dotfiles/scripts/setup-steam-matugen.sh

It validates dependencies, clones Adwaita-for-Steam once, links the custom stylesheet, renders the palette with the same flags as apply-matugen.sh, injects the theme, and prints a verification report.

docs.title: Manual Installation: Adwaita-for-Steam Theme Integration
docs.text:
Standalone instructions to add the Steam theme integration to an existing matugen installation without cloning the full dotfiles repository. This follows the manual installation format pioneered in Matugen (VS Code pilot).

All snippets are compatible with bash and zsh, use explicit quoted paths, and are safe to paste into an interactive shell.

docs.title: Step 1: Validate prerequisites
docs.text:
Run the checks. Every line must report OK before continuing:

command -v steam >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "steam         : OK" || echo "steam         : MISSING"
test -d "$HOME/.steam/steam" && echo "steam dir     : OK" || echo "steam dir     : MISSING"
command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "python3       : OK" || echo "python3       : MISSING"
command -v git >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "git           : OK" || echo "git           : MISSING"
command -v matugen >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "matugen       : OK" || echo "matugen       : MISSING"
test -d "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates" && echo "templates dir : OK" || echo "templates dir : MISSING"
test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" && echo "config.toml   : OK" || echo "config.toml   : MISSING"

If a line reports MISSING:

  • steam / steam dir: install the native Steam client (apt install steam on Debian) or skip this integration.
  • python3: install it with your package manager (apt install python3 on Debian).
  • git: install it with your package manager (apt install git on Debian).
  • matugen: install it from https://github.com/InioX/matugen.
  • templates dir: create it with mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates".
  • config.toml: create an empty one with touch "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml".

docs.title: Step 2: Back up the files that will be modified
docs.text:
The only existing files altered by this procedure are config.toml and, when a previous clone already exists, its custom/custom.css. Backups carry the exact date and time of the operation:

BACKUP_STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" && cp -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"
test -f "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam/custom/custom.css" && cp -p "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam/custom/custom.css" "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam/custom/custom.css.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"
echo "Backups created with stamp: $BACKUP_STAMP"

The template file from a previous attempt is backed up the same way before being replaced:

test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/steam.css" && cp -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/steam.css" "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/steam.css.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"

docs.title: Step 3: Create the template file
docs.text:
Download it directly from the repository:

mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates"
curl -fsSL -o "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/steam.css" "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zer0sh/dotfiles/main/matugen/templates/steam.css"

Alternatively, copy the contents manually from steam.css into the destination path shown above.

Confirm the file exists and is not empty:

test -s "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/steam.css" && echo "steam.css : OK" || echo "steam.css : MISSING"

docs.title: Step 4: Register the template in config.toml
docs.text:
The block below is idempotent: it appends the section only when it is not already registered, and the heredoc delimiter is quoted, so no shell expansion happens inside it:

if grep -q "^\[templates.steam\]" "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml"; then
    echo "Already registered in config.toml, nothing to do."
else
    cat >> "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" <<'EOF'

# Steam (Adwaita-for-Steam install.py injects the rendered palette)
[templates.steam]
input_path = "~/.config/matugen/templates/steam.css"
output_path = "~/.config/themes/current/steam.css"
post_hook = 'cd "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam" && python3 install.py --custom-css -t normal >/dev/null 2>&1 || true'
EOF
    echo "Registered in config.toml."
fi

If an older [templates.steam] block exists with an adwaita-steam-gtk or flatpak run hook, edit that post_hook line and replace it with the one above.

docs.title: Step 5: Clone Adwaita-for-Steam and link the custom stylesheet
docs.text:
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/share"
test -d "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam" || git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/Foldex/Adwaita-for-Steam.git "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam"
mkdir -p "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam/custom"
ln -sf "$HOME/.config/themes/current/steam.css" "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam/custom/custom.css"

This replaces the example custom/custom.css shipped by the repository (preserved by the Step 2 backup if it contained custom content). The installer dereferences the symlink while staging, so the clone always carries the current palette without further intervention.

docs.title: Step 6: Generate the colors
docs.text:
WALLPAPER="$(cat "$HOME/.config/themes/current/wallpaper" 2>/dev/null || true)"
MODE="$(cat "$HOME/.config/themes/current/mode" 2>/dev/null || echo dark)"
if [ -n "$WALLPAPER" ] && [ -f "$WALLPAPER" ]; then
    matugen image "$WALLPAPER" \
        --config "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" \
        -t scheme-vibrant --contrast 0.2 \
        --mode "$MODE" --source-color-index 0 --quiet
else
    echo "No active wallpaper in the theme store yet; run themes/apply-matugen.sh first."
fi
test -s "$HOME/.config/themes/current/steam.css" && echo "steam.css : OK" || echo "steam.css : MISSING"

The flags mirror ~/dotfiles/themes/apply-matugen.sh; --source-color-index 0 bypasses the interactive color picker.

docs.title: Step 7: Inject the theme into Steam
docs.text:
Run the installer from its repository root (the subshell keeps your current directory unchanged):

( cd "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam" && python3 install.py --custom-css -t normal )

Expected output includes Applying custom css..., Patching Steam Client Library Files... and Done!. On the first run the installer renames the pristine steamui/css/library.css to library.original.css and replaces it with an @import wrapper of the same byte size.

docs.title: Step 8: Restart Steam and verify
docs.text:
Exit Steam completely (including the tray icon) and launch it again, then run:

grep -q "^/\*patched\*/" "$HOME/.local/share/Steam/steamui/css/library.css" && echo "library patch : OK" || echo "library patch : MISSING"
grep -q "custom/custom.css" "$HOME/.local/share/Steam/steamui/libraryroot.custom.css" && echo "custom import : OK" || echo "custom import : MISSING"
grep -q "adw-accent-rgb" "$HOME/.local/share/Steam/steamui/adwaita/custom/custom.css" && echo "palette copy  : OK" || echo "palette copy  : MISSING"

All three lines must report OK, and the Steam Library must display the wallpaper-derived palette after the restart.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Theme not visible: Steam loads its stylesheets at startup. Exit the client completely (tray included) and launch it again.
  • Steam updated and the theme disappeared: Steam restores library.css during client updates. Re-run Step 7 (or the setup script); every wallpaper change also re-applies the theme automatically through the post_hook.
  • install.py reports that the theme directory does not exist: the command was not run from the clone root. Use the subshell form of Step 7.
  • Colors missing or invalid: verify the symlink (readlink -f "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam/custom/custom.css") and that themes/current/steam.css contains comma-separated triplets such as --adw-accent-rgb: 158, 217, 0;.
  • Revert to the Steam default appearance:
( cd "$HOME/.local/share/Adwaita-for-Steam" && python3 install.py --uninstall -t normal )

This empties libraryroot.custom.css and removes the steamui/adwaita/ copy; library.css stays as the harmless @import wrapper pointing at library.original.css.

docs.title: Real-time Wallpaper Synchronization
docs.text: When wallpaper transitions occur via Quickshell launcher or control center, matugen image renders all templates. The configured post_hook silently runs install.py --custom-css -t normal, so the Steam clone and the steamui folder always receive the fresh palette without manual intervention. The Steam client itself must be restarted to display the refreshed colors; there is no supported hot reload outside of Steam's -dev mode.

docs.title: Optional: AdwSteamGtk Graphical Wrapper
docs.text:
AdwSteamGtk is a GTK front-end for the same theme. It is not required by this pipeline and is only distributed as a Flatpak:

flatpak install flathub io.github.Foldex.AdwSteamGtk

If it is installed, install.sh additionally links the central store output to its custom stylesheet locations (~/.config/AdwSteamGtk/custom.css and the Flatpak equivalent), and Preferences -> Custom CSS must be enabled inside the application for those links to be honored. The native install.py route described above keeps working independently of this wrapper.

docs.title: Optional: Millennium Modding Framework
docs.text:
Millennium (SteamClientHomebrew, MIT) is an open-source modding framework that loads custom themes and plugins into the Steam UI. It is listed as an optional requirement of this setup: the matugen/Adwaita-for-Steam pipeline works without it, because both operate on different layers:

  • Adwaita-for-Steam patches steamui/css/library.css and serves stylesheets through https://steamloopback.host.
  • Millennium LD-preloads its shared objects into steamwebhelper to inject the JavaScript and plugin layer.

The two have been validated together on this setup without conflicts.

docs.title: Installation (Debian and other distributions)
docs.text:
The official installer downloads the latest stable release from GitHub and verifies its sha256 checksum. It requires sudo for /usr/lib/millennium (and refuses to run as root) plus one i386 prerequisite on Debian:

sudo dpkg --add-architecture i386 && sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y libssl-dev:i386
curl -fsSL "https://steambrew.app/install.sh" | bash

Confirm the prompt, then restart Steam completely so the new shared objects are loaded. Arch Linux users can install the millennium AUR package instead; Flatpak and Snap Steam are not supported by Millennium.

docs.title: Paths touched by Millennium
docs.text: Path Owner Content /usr/lib/millennium/*.so root Bootstrap and preload shared objects (system layer) ~/.steam/steam/ubuntu12_32/libXtst.so.6, ~/.steam/steam/ubuntu12_64/libXtst.so.6 user Preload symlinks created by the installer ~/.local/share/millennium/ user themes/, plugins/ and the plugin ~/.venv ~/.steam/steam/package/beta user Removed by the installer (forces the stable Steam channel)

docs.title: Updating and uninstalling
docs.text: Re-run the installer command above to update to the latest stable release, and restart Steam afterwards. Removal instructions live in the official Uninstalling guide.

docs.title: Waybar Status Bar
docs.text: Waybar serves as the primary top status bar in this desktop environment, engineered with a ChromeOS Shelf aesthetic, rounded capsule pills, and seamless IPC communication with Quickshell and the Hyprland compositor.

docs.title: Architecture and File Map
docs.text:
• Live symlink: ~/.config/waybar -> ~/dotfiles/waybar
  • Configuration: ~/.config/waybar/config.jsonc (module layout and actions)
  • Stylesheet: ~/.config/waybar/style.css (visual properties and ChromeOS pill styling)
  • Dynamic Palette: ~/.config/waybar/colors.css (imports ~/.config/themes/current/waybar.css generated by Matugen)
  • Helper Scripts:
    • ~/.config/waybar/scripts/notifications: Reads real-time notification queue state
    • ~/.config/waybar/scripts/mediaplayer: MPRIS playback monitor with 40-character ticker marquee and Quickshell Dynamic Island integration
    • ~/.config/waybar/scripts/powerprofile: Real-time power profiles daemon monitor and toggle (power-saver, balanced, performance)

docs.title: Layout and Modules
docs.text:
Waybar is docked at the top of the display with a height of 36 pixels and an accented 2 px bottom border (border-radius: 0; border-bottom: 2px solid @accent;) engineered for seamless, organic Dynamic Island integration with Quickshell dropdown panels:

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| [Launcher] [Workspaces]               [Now Playing Pill]                [Tray] [Notifs] [Unified System Pill] |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 1. Left Section
docs.text:
• custom/launcher: Circular action button styled after the ChromeOS app launcher. Clicking executes qs ipc call launcher toggle to display the Quickshell application drawer.
  • hyprland/workspaces: Pill container with dynamic indicators. Inactive workspaces appear as muted capsule pills, while the active workspace morphs into an accented circular indicator.

docs.title: 2. Center Section
docs.text:
• custom/media: Centralized ChromeOS capsule pill (border-radius: 18px, min-width: 260px, background: alpha(@text, 0.08)) displaying currently playing media with a smooth 40-character marquee ticker:
    • Marquee Dynamics: Automatically rotates long track titles (0.5s steps) with clean loop separation (•), freezing cleanly in place upon pause and collapsing completely (.empty) when no media is active.
    • Left Click: Executes qs ipc call mediaselector toggle, smoothly opening the Quickshell Dynamic Island media source dropdown.
    • Right Click: Toggles play/pause state via playerctl play-pause.
    • Mouse Scroll: Navigates tracks via playerctl next (scroll up) and playerctl previous (scroll down).
    • Global Tooltips: Clean, non-intrusive status tooltip (Playing... / Paused...) styled globally with Matugen-themed container colors and rounded corners (border-radius: 12px).

docs.title: 3. Right Section
docs.text:
• tray: Wayland system tray for background application icons (icon-size: 14px, spacing: 8px). The container collapses to zero width and margins when empty, rendering active icons inside rounded capsule badges (border-radius: 14px, background: alpha(@text, 0.08)).
  • Quick Actions & Notifications Pill (group/quick_actions):
    • Unified capsule pill hosting quick hardware indicators alongside the notification bell and clipboard manager (custom/caffeine, custom/nightlight, custom/shader, custom/powerprofile, custom/notifications, custom/clipboard).
    • Empty state collapse: When all quick toggles are inactive, the pill seamlessly scales to contain solely the notification bell and clipboard button, eliminating any residual empty container spacing or layout shifts.
    • Active indicators: When one or more toggles are engaged, their accented glyphs (color: @accent, font-size: 16px) appear inline to the left of the notification bell, sharing the unified capsule container (border-radius: 18px, background: alpha(@text, 0.08)).
    • custom/caffeine: Displays coffee cup glyph (󰅶) when session wake-lock is engaged via POSIX signal SIGRTMIN+8.
    • custom/nightlight: Displays eye glyph (󰈈) when hyprsunset warm light filter (4000K) is active via POSIX signal SIGRTMIN+9.
    • custom/shader: Displays screen shader glyph (󰸉) when screen decoration shader is applied via POSIX signal SIGRTMIN+10.
    • custom/powerprofile: Displays active power profile glyphs when operating outside the balanced default: leaf glyph (󰌪) for power-saver or speedometer glyph (󰓅) for performance. Completely collapses in balanced mode. Synchronizes instantly via POSIX signal SIGRTMIN+11 from Quickshell Control Center and power profile daemon events. Left click cycles profiles; right click opens the Quickshell Energy & Performance dashboard.
    • custom/notifications: Notification bell integrated with Quickshell Notification Service and DND state:
      • Displays standard bell glyph (󰂚) in neutral text color (@text) when notification history is empty.
      • Displays bell glyph with unread count (󰂚 [N]) highlighted in accent color (@accent) when notifications are pending.
      • Morphs dynamically into the Do Not Disturb glyph (󰂛 [N] or 󰂛) highlighted in accent color (@accent) when DND mode is enabled.
      • Synchronizes in real time via POSIX signal SIGRTMIN+1.
      • Left click invokes qs ipc call notifications toggle, opening the Control Center with the notifications card expanded.
    • custom/clipboard: Clipboard manager action button displaying clip glyph (󰅌). Left click invokes qs ipc call clipboard toggle, opening the Quickshell bottom-sliding Clipboard Manager.
  • Unified Status Pill: Merged continuous capsule pill containing date, time, audio, network, bluetooth, and battery/power:
    • custom/date: Formatted date (date +'%b %d'), styled as the rounded left edge of the unified pill.
    • clock: Local time format {:%H:%M} with bold typography.
    • pulseaudio: Volume glyphs; click toggles Quickshell Control Center, right-click opens pavucontrol, and mouse wheel scrolling adjusts sink volume using wpctl set-volume.
    • network: Wi-Fi / Ethernet state; click opens Quickshell Control Center.
    • bluetooth: Adapter state and connection count; click opens Quickshell Control Center. Features an optical size increase (18px) when active, and collapses to zero width (format-disabled: "" and format-off: "") when Bluetooth is powered off.
    • battery / custom/power: Charge percentage, charging animations, and battery warnings (laptop) or power state (desktop), styled as the rounded right edge of the unified pill.

docs.title: Integration with Quickshell and Hyprland
docs.text:
Waybar and Quickshell operate in synchronized coexistence:

  1. Vertical Hierarchy:
  2. Waybar occupies the top 36 pixels (height: 36, layer: top).
  3. Quickshell floating toasts and OSDs reserve a topMargin: 46 px, creating an aligned 10 px air gap directly below Waybar's rounded bottom border (see Notifications & OSDs).
  4. IPC Interactivity:
  5. Clicking audio, network, or bluetooth indicators directly opens the One UI Control Center inside Quickshell.
  6. Clicking the launcher circle opens the Quickshell app search matrix without requiring full-screen interruptions.
  7. Real-time Signal Sync (SIGRTMIN+1):
  8. Quickshell writes unread counts to /tmp/qs-notif-count and issues pkill -RTMIN+1 waybar, triggering immediate redraws without CPU polling overhead.

docs.title: Dynamic Palette Integration (Matugen)
docs.text:
Colors and translucency tokens are imported dynamically from the centralized theme store:

/* ~/.config/waybar/colors.css */
@import url("/home/zero/.config/themes/current/waybar.css");

  • @text: Primary typography and icon color.
  • @accent: Active workspace indicator and highlight borders.
  • @warning: Battery low threshold (<= 30%).
  • @critical: Battery critical threshold (<= 10%).
  • @charging: Battery active power supply state.

pkill -SIGUSR2 waybar

docs.title: Zen Browser Dynamic Theming
docs.text: Zen Browser is integrated into the dynamic Material You theming pipeline using Matugen templates. The templates render harmonic colors extracted from the active wallpaper into the browser profile, covering the browser chrome (sidebar, tabs, toolbar, urlbar, panels, menus) and the internal about: pages. The templates are adapted from the InioX/matugen-themes Zen Browser section (MIT license).

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Requirement Minimum Purpose Validate with Zen Browser 1.14 or newer Firefox-based browser with a profile at ~/.zen zen --version matugen 4.x Renders the Material Design 3 palette from a wallpaper command -v matugen Matugen engine config any Provides ~/.config/matugen/config.toml and ~/.config/matugen/templates/ test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" curl any Downloads the templates (manual installation only) command -v curl bash or zsh any Runs the snippets of this guide echo $0 Profile stylesheet pref true Loads userChrome.css / userContent.css (off by default since Zen 1.14) about:config entry toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets Window transparency pref true Allows transparent background for Hyprland system blur about:config entry browser.tabs.allow_transparent_browser

No sudo privileges are required. The integration does not modify browser binaries or installation directories; it only touches files inside the user profile and the matugen configuration.

docs.title: File Structure and Paths
docs.text:
Action Path Notes Create ~/dotfiles/matugen/templates/zen-userchrome.css Chrome UI template (source of truth in the repository) Create ~/dotfiles/matugen/templates/zen-usercontent.css Internal about: pages template Modify (backup first) ~/dotfiles/matugen/config.toml Registers [templates.zen-userchrome] and [templates.zen-usercontent] Create (rendered by matugen) ~/.zen/xbjonc67.Default Profile/chrome/zen-userChrome.css Output of the chrome template Create (rendered by matugen) ~/.zen/xbjonc67.Default Profile/chrome/zen-userContent.css Output of the content template Create (entry file) ~/.zen/xbjonc67.Default Profile/chrome/userChrome.css Single @import line pointing at the rendered chrome file Create (entry file) ~/.zen/xbjonc67.Default Profile/chrome/userContent.css Single @import line pointing at the rendered content file Modify (append) ~/.zen/xbjonc67.Default Profile/user.js Enables stylesheets and transparent window prefs Create ~/dotfiles/scripts/setup-zen-matugen.sh Deployment and verification automation Modify ~/dotfiles/install.sh Runs the setup script when Zen Browser is detected

The profile folder name (xbjonc67.Default Profile) is specific to this machine. Resolve the active profile of any installation with:

grep -E "^Path=|^IsRelative=|^Default=1" "$HOME/.zen/profiles.ini"

Note: unlike every other consumer, the Zen outputs are rendered directly into the profile chrome/ folder instead of ~/.config/themes/current/, because Zen (like every Firefox fork) only loads stylesheets from the profile. The generated files are plain static CSS, so nothing else consumes the central theme store for this target.

docs.title: Chrome template (zen-userchrome.css)
docs.text: Feature / Element Implementation Details System Blur & Transparency Semi-transparent backgrounds (color-mix with colors.background.default at 72-78%) with backdrop-filter: blur(20px) for Hyprland integration. Material You Active Tabs Active tab pill (border-radius: 20px) filled with colors.primary_container.default and bold colors.on_primary_container.default text. Tab Controls & New Tab Pill-shaped new tab button (border-radius: 20px) with aligned margins and smooth hover transitions. Unified URL & Search Bar Matches top bar background (colors.background.default mix) with var(--zen-border-radius, 10px) geometry and an active colors.primary.default border. docs.title: Content template (zen-usercontent.css)
docs.text:
• Default Dynamic Hyperlinks: Global :where(:link) and :where(:visited) anchors automatically inherit the wallpaper accent tone (colors.primary.default) on unstyled websites without overriding custom page CSS.
  • Internal about: Pages: Full Material Design 3 token overrides for about:preferences, about:addons, about:config, about:logins, about:support, about:home, about:newtab, and about:blank.

docs.title: Reload Strategy
docs.text:
userChrome.css and userContent.css are read only at browser startup. After every wallpaper change the palette is regenerated automatically, but Zen must be fully restarted to display it:

  1. Close every Zen window (the process must exit completely).
  2. Open Zen again from the application launcher.

An in-app relaunch (about:profiles restart or the built-in restart action) is known to leave stale stylesheets in some Zen releases; a manual full restart is the reliable method.

docs.title: Automatic Installation (Dotfiles)
docs.text:
The integration is deployed by the standard dotfiles routine:

~/dotfiles/install.sh

Or manually at any time with the standalone script:

~/dotfiles/scripts/setup-zen-matugen.sh

The script resolves the default profile from profiles.ini (native and Flatpak installations are supported), creates the chrome/ folder, backs up and patches the entry files, enables the stylesheet preference in user.js, regenerates the palette from the stored wallpaper, and prints a verification report. It is idempotent: running it twice never duplicates the @import lines or the preference.

docs.title: Manual Installation: Zen Browser Theme Integration
docs.text:
Standalone instructions to add the Zen Browser theme integration to an existing matugen installation without cloning the full dotfiles repository. This is the second application of the manual installation format pioneered in Matugen (VS Code pilot).

All snippets are compatible with bash and zsh, use explicit paths (no glob patterns), quote every path (Zen profile folders usually contain spaces), and are safe to paste into an interactive shell.

docs.title: Step 1: Validate prerequisites
docs.text:
Run the checks. Every line must report OK before continuing. The preference used to load profile stylesheets is validated in Step 7:

command -v matugen >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "matugen       : OK" || echo "matugen       : MISSING"
command -v curl >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "curl          : OK" || echo "curl          : MISSING"
test -f "$HOME/.zen/profiles.ini" && echo "zen registry  : OK" || echo "zen registry  : MISSING"
test -d "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates" && echo "templates dir : OK" || echo "templates dir : MISSING"
test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" && echo "config.toml   : OK" || echo "config.toml   : MISSING"
echo "profile pref  : CHECK MANUALLY (expected MISSING, Step 7 enables it)"

The profile stylesheet preference (toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets) lives inside the profile, which is resolved in Step 2, so it is validated there instead.

If a line reports MISSING:

  • matugen: install it from https://github.com/InioX/matugen.
  • curl: install it with your package manager (apt install curl on Debian).
  • zen registry: install Zen Browser, or create the file with touch "$HOME/.zen/profiles.ini" only if you manage the profile manually.
  • templates dir: create it with mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates".
  • config.toml: create an empty one with touch "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml".

docs.title: Step 2: Locate the active profile
docs.text:
grep -E "^Path=|^IsRelative=|^Default=1" "$HOME/.zen/profiles.ini"

Identify the Path= value of the block marked with Default=1. From this point on, replace <profile-path> in every snippet with that value, keeping the double quotes (profile names contain spaces). Example for this machine:

PROFILE_DIR="$HOME/.zen/xbjonc67.Default Profile"
test -d "$PROFILE_DIR" && echo "profile dir   : OK" || echo "profile dir   : MISSING"

docs.title: Step 3: Back up the files that will be modified
docs.text:
The only existing files altered by this procedure are config.toml, the entry files (userChrome.css / userContent.css, when they already exist) and user.js. Backups carry the exact date and time of the operation:

BACKUP_STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" && cp -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"
test -f "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/userChrome.css" && cp -p "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/userChrome.css" "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/userChrome.css.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"
test -f "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/userContent.css" && cp -p "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/userContent.css" "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/userContent.css.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"
test -f "$PROFILE_DIR/user.js" && cp -p "$PROFILE_DIR/user.js" "$PROFILE_DIR/user.js.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"
echo "Backups created with stamp: $BACKUP_STAMP"

If template files from a previous attempt already exist, they are backed up the same way before being replaced:

test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/zen-userchrome.css" && cp -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/zen-userchrome.css" "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/zen-userchrome.css.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"
test -f "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/zen-usercontent.css" && cp -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/zen-usercontent.css" "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/zen-usercontent.css.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"

docs.title: Step 4: Create the template files
docs.text:
Download both templates directly from the repository:

mkdir -p "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates"
curl -fsSL -o "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/zen-userchrome.css" "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zer0sh/dotfiles/main/matugen/templates/zen-userchrome.css"
curl -fsSL -o "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/zen-usercontent.css" "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/zer0sh/dotfiles/main/matugen/templates/zen-usercontent.css"

Alternatively, copy the file contents manually from the repository pages (zen-userchrome.css, zen-usercontent.css) into the destination paths shown above.

Confirm both files exist and are not empty:

test -s "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/zen-userchrome.css" && echo "zen-userchrome.css : OK" || echo "zen-userchrome.css : MISSING"
test -s "$HOME/.config/matugen/templates/zen-usercontent.css" && echo "zen-usercontent.css : OK" || echo "zen-usercontent.css : MISSING"

docs.title: Step 5: Register the templates in config.toml
docs.text:
Edit the block below before pasting it: replace both occurrences of <profile-path> with the value obtained in Step 2. The block is idempotent: it appends the sections only when they are not already registered, and the heredoc delimiter is quoted, so no variable or shell expansion happens inside it:

if grep -q "^\[templates.zen-userchrome\]" "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml"; then
    echo "Already registered in config.toml, nothing to do."
else
    cat >> "$HOME/.config/matugen/config.toml" <<'EOF'

# Zen Browser (imported by <profile>/chrome/userChrome.css and userContent.css)
[templates.zen-userchrome]
input_path = "~/.config/matugen/templates/zen-userchrome.css"
output_path = "~/.zen/<profile-path>/chrome/zen-userChrome.css"

[templates.zen-usercontent]
input_path = "~/.config/matugen/templates/zen-usercontent.css"
output_path = "~/.zen/<profile-path>/chrome/zen-userContent.css"
EOF
    echo "Registered in config.toml."
fi

docs.title: Step 6: Create the chrome/ folder and the entry files
docs.text:
The entry files contain a single @import each, pointing at the rendered template with an absolute path. Relative imports are ignored by Firefox style sheets, so the path must start with /home/<user>:

mkdir -p "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome"
BACKUP_STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S)"
for entry in userChrome.css userContent.css; do
    target="zen-$entry"
    import_line="$(printf '@import url("%s");' "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/$target")"
    if [ -f "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/$entry" ] && grep -Fq "$target" "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/$entry"; then
        echo "$entry already imports $target."
    elif [ -f "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/$entry" ]; then
        cp -p "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/$entry" "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/$entry.$BACKUP_STAMP.bak"
        printf '%s\n%s\n' "$import_line" "$(cat "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/$entry")" > "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/$entry"
        echo "Updated $entry (backup created)."
    else
        printf '%s\n' "$import_line" > "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/$entry"
        echo "Created $entry."
    fi
done

The import line is prepended because CSS ignores @import rules placed after any style rule. Personal customizations that already exist in the entry files are preserved below the import.

docs.title: Step 7: Enable the profile stylesheet preference
docs.text:
Zen disables profile stylesheets by default since v1.14 (aligned with the Firefox default). Either toggle it in the browser:

  1. Open about:config in the address bar.
  2. Search for toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets.
  3. Set it to true.

or persist it from the shell (the user.js file is re-applied on every startup, so the preference can never be flipped back by an update):

PREF='toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets'
if grep -Fq "\"$PREF\", true" "$PROFILE_DIR/user.js" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "Preference already enabled in user.js."
else
    printf 'user_pref("%s", true);\n' "$PREF" >> "$PROFILE_DIR/user.js"
    echo "Preference appended to user.js."
fi

docs.title: Step 8: Generate the colors
docs.text:
Replace the wallpaper path with your own absolute path. The --source-color-index 0 flag disables the interactive color picker, so the command also works from keybindings or non-interactive shells:

matugen image "/absolute/path/to/your-wallpaper.jpg" --mode dark --source-color-index 0
test -f "$HOME/.zen/xbjonc67.Default Profile/chrome/zen-userChrome.css" && echo "rendered chrome  : OK" || echo "rendered chrome  : MISSING"
test -f "$HOME/.zen/xbjonc67.Default Profile/chrome/zen-userContent.css" && echo "rendered content : OK" || echo "rendered content : MISSING"

Adjust <profile-path> in both paths if your profile folder differs.

docs.title: Step 9: Restart Zen Browser
docs.text: Close every Zen window and open it again from the application launcher. The theme is applied at startup only.

docs.title: Step 10: Verification
docs.text:
test -s "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/zen-userChrome.css" && echo "chrome file   : OK" || echo "chrome file   : MISSING"
test -s "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/zen-userContent.css" && echo "content file  : OK" || echo "content file  : MISSING"
grep -Fq "zen-userChrome.css" "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/userChrome.css" && echo "chrome import : OK" || echo "chrome import : MISSING"
grep -Fq "zen-userContent.css" "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/userContent.css" && echo "content import: OK" || echo "content import: MISSING"
grep -Fq "\"toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets\", true" "$PROFILE_DIR/user.js" 2>/dev/null && echo "preference    : OK" || echo "preference    : MISSING (or set manually in about:config)"
grep -q "{{" "$PROFILE_DIR/chrome/zen-userChrome.css" 2>/dev/null && echo "rendered css  : TEMPLATE VARIABLES LEFT" || echo "rendered css  : OK"

The last check reports TEMPLATE VARIABLES LEFT when matugen has not processed the templates yet; run Step 8 again in that case.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
• Nothing changed after the restart: open about:config and confirm that toolkit.legacyUserProfileCustomizations.stylesheets is true. If it was toggled after the browser was opened, restart Zen completely (close every window instead of using an in-app relaunch, which is known to keep stale stylesheets in some releases).
  • The import has no effect: verify that the @import line is the first statement of userChrome.css / userContent.css. Imports placed after a style rule are ignored by the CSS specification.
  • Colors did not change after a wallpaper switch: run Step 8 again and confirm the output paths registered in config.toml match your profile folder exactly, including spaces.
  • Template placeholders visible in the rendered file: the output_path registered in config.toml does not match the file imported by the entry files; fix the path and regenerate.
  • Inspect the applied styles: press Ctrl+Alt+Shift+I to open the Browser Toolbox and check that zen-userChrome.css is listed in the style editor.
  • Restore the previous configuration: copy the backups created in Steps 3 and 6 back over the original files using the exact names printed by the backup commands, then restart Zen.

docs.title: Release Management & SemVer
docs.text: This repository follows Semantic Versioning 2.0.0 (vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH) and Conventional Commits to automate versioning, release artifacts, and documentation deployment.

docs.title: Versioning Scheme
docs.text:
• MAJOR (vX.0.0): Incompatible architectural overhauls (e.g. switching compositor, complete directory reshuffling).
  • MINOR (v1.X.0): New features, widgets, or apps added backward-compatibly (e.g. adding an OCR tool, new Quickshell modules).
  • PATCH (v1.0.X): Backward-compatible bug fixes, minor CSS styling tweaks, or performance optimizations.

docs.title: How to Trigger a Release
docs.text: You have two convenient ways to cut a new release:

docs.title: Option 1: From Your Terminal (CLI Helper)
docs.text:
Run the included release script in the repository:

# Interactive mode (prompts for patch, minor, major, or custom)
./scripts/release.sh

# Or directly specify the bump type:
./scripts/release.sh patch   # e.g. v1.0.0 -> v1.0.1
./scripts/release.sh minor   # e.g. v1.0.0 -> v1.1.0
./scripts/release.sh major   # e.g. v1.0.0 -> v2.0.0
./scripts/release.sh v1.0.0  # explicit version

The script will: 1. Verify that your git working tree is clean. 2. Determine the next SemVer tag. 3. Create the annotated git tag. 4. Push both main and the new tag to GitHub.

docs.title: Option 2: From GitHub Actions (Web UI)
docs.text:
1. Navigate to your repository on GitHub: https://github.com/zer0sh/dotfiles/actions.
  2. Select the Release & Deploy workflow on the left sidebar.
  3. Click Run workflow.
  4. Choose the bump type (patch, minor, major) or enter a custom version.
  5. Click the green Run workflow button.

docs.title: Automated Pipeline (What Happens on Release)
docs.text:
When a release tag is pushed (v*.*.*):

flowchart LR
    A["Git Tag (v1.0.0)"] --> B["GitHub Actions"]
    B --> C["Package Archives (.tar.gz & .zip)"]
    B --> D["Generate Release Notes (Conventional Commits)"]
    C --> E["Publish GitHub Release"]
    D --> E
    E --> F["Deploy Wiki to GitHub Pages"]
  1. Release Notes: GitHub automatically categorizes commits into Features, Bug Fixes, and Maintenance based on Conventional Commits.
  2. Packaged Assets: Generates clean dotfiles-vX.Y.Z.tar.gz and dotfiles-vX.Y.Z.zip archives attached to the release for easy distribution or disaster recovery.
  3. Wiki Deployment: Compiles and deploys the latest MkDocs documentation to zer0sh.github.io/dotfiles.

docs.title: Dotfiles Workflow & Architecture
docs.text: This guide explains how configuration files are structured between your active system and the version-controlled repository on GitHub.

docs.title: Direct Source of Truth Philosophy
docs.text:
• Hyprland: ~/.config/hypr is a real physical directory (not a symlink). You can edit configuration files directly in place without risk of symlink breakage or intermediate layer issues (see Hyprland Architecture).
  • Quickshell: ~/.config/quickshell is also maintained directly on the system for instant QML hot-reloading (see Quickshell Overview).
  • Dotfiles Repository: ~/dotfiles serves as the Git repository and backup hub connected to github.com/zer0sh/dotfiles.
  • Symlinked Applications: Modular components like Alacritty, Zsh, and Fastfetch link their active system paths directly to ~/dotfiles/.

docs.title: How to Backup Hyprland Changes
docs.text:
Whenever you test and stabilize adjustments in your Hyprland configuration and want to commit them to your repository:

  1. Copy live configuration into the dotfiles directory: 
    cp -r ~/.config/hypr/* ~/dotfiles/hypr/
  2. Review diffs and create atomic commits: Follow Conventional Commits standards as documented in Release Management & SemVer: 
    cd ~/dotfiles
git status
git add hypr/
git commit -m "feat(hypr): describe your changes"
  3. Push to GitHub: 
    git push origin main

docs.text:
To preview the documentation locally with live-reload:

cd ~/dotfiles
mkdocs serve

To build and deploy changes directly to GitHub Pages:

cd ~/dotfiles
mkdocs gh-deploy

(Note: Pushing to main also automatically triggers the GitHub Actions workflow defined in .github/workflows/deploy-docs.yml, as detailed in Release Management & SemVer).
