docs.text: The documentation uses Material for MkDocs enhanced with custom Material 3 and Glassmorphism styling (docs/stylesheets/extra.css): * Right-Hand Primary Navigation: The navigation sidebar tree is docked on the right side on desktop viewport sizes (min-width: 76.25em), presenting page hierarchy inside a frosted glass card (backdrop-filter: blur(14px)). * Precise Active Indicators: Parent section headers remain in clean bold text without intrusive highlight boxes, while only the active target page receives the active accent container pill. * Responsive Drawer: On mobile devices, the navigation switches to a left slide-out Material You navigation drawer triggered from the top app bar.

docs.title: Hyprland Architecture
docs.text: Hyprland is organized using a strict modular approach. The primary hyprland.conf does not define keybindings or individual properties directly; it acts exclusively as an orchestrator using source = directives.

docs.title: Directory & File Structure
docs.text:
~/.config/hypr/
├── hyprland.conf         # Master entrypoint (imports sub-modules only)
├── binds.conf            # Keyboard shortcuts and mouse actions
├── monitors.conf         # Screen layouts and refresh rates (nwg-displays)
├── workspaces.conf       # Virtual desktop allocations
├── autostart.conf        # Startup services and daemons (exec-once)
├── animations.conf       # Bezier curves and window movement dynamics
├── decoration.conf       # Borders, shadows, blur, and gaps
├── miscellaneous.conf    # Keyboard repeat rate and layout behavior
├── window.conf           # Window rules & XWayland fixes (see xwayland.md)
├── hyprlock.conf         # Lock screen layout and theming
├── hypridle.conf         # Idle management and power saving
├── scripts/              # Executable shell helpers (OCR, screenshots, filters)
└── shaders/              # Custom GLSL post-processing shaders

docs.title: Master Entrypoint (hyprland.conf)
docs.text:
# Monitor layout managed by nwg-displays
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/monitors.conf

source = $HOME/.config/hypr/variables.conf
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/binds.conf
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/window.conf
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/decoration.conf

# Centralized palette generated by the active theme
source = $HOME/.config/themes/current/hyprland.conf

source = $HOME/.config/hypr/animations.conf
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/miscellaneous.conf
source = $HOME/.config/hypr/autostart.conf

docs.title: Startup Services (autostart.conf)
docs.text:
• Quickshell: Loads desktop widgets, top-center OSD layers & notifications, and the One UI control center.
  • Waybar: Top system status bar running alongside Quickshell widgets.
  • Polkit Agent: systemctl --user start hyprpolkitagent for GUI privilege escalation.
  • Cliphist: Text and image clipboard history daemons integrated with Quickshell clipboard drawer.
  • Wallpaper & Theme: Automatic restoration via $HOME/.config/hypr/scripts/restore-wallpaper and Matugen theming engine.
  • Desktop Environment Sync: dbus-update-activation-environment and systemctl --user import-environment for WAYLAND_DISPLAY and XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP.
  • Battery & Charger Monitor: Real-time daemon $HOME/.config/hypr/scripts/battery-notify monitoring AC connection/disconnection and dispatching 20% / 10% low battery notifications.

docs.title: Desktop Portals & GNOME App Latency
docs.text: Applications built on GTK4 and Libadwaita (Nautilus, GNOME Calculator, Text Editor, Loupe) may experience a severe startup delay (~3.5 seconds) if portal backends are improperly prioritized.

docs.title: Cause of Delay
docs.text: xdg-desktop-portal-gnome expects GNOME Shell and Mutter services on D-Bus. When running under Hyprland, these services do not exist, causing D-Bus calls to hang until reaching their timeout. Masking the systemd service alone is insufficient because D-Bus service activation files (/usr/share/dbus-1/services/) still trigger queries.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
1. Purge GNOME Portal Backend: 
    sudo apt remove --purge xdg-desktop-portal-gnome
  2. Configure Preferred Portals (~/.config/xdg-desktop-portal/portals.conf): 
    [preferred]
default=hyprland;gtk
  3. Environment Activation (autostart.conf): 
    exec-once = dbus-update-activation-environment --systemd WAYLAND_DISPLAY XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP
exec-once = systemctl --user import-environment WAYLAND_DISPLAY XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP

  • Hypridle configuration: ~/dotfiles/hypr/hypridle.conf -> ~/.config/hypr/hypridle.conf

docs.title: Hyprlock Architecture
docs.text: Hyprlock generates a real-time frosted glass lock screen that adapts dynamically to the current wallpaper and active Material You color palette.

docs.title: 1. Dynamic Theming (Matugen Integration)
docs.text:
Color tokens are evaluated by Matugen and imported directly into hyprlock.conf:

source = /home/zero/.config/themes/current/hyprlock.conf

Available color roles include: * $accentColorPurple: Primary accent used for borders and validation states. * $bgColorSecondary: Inner background container for the input field. * $textColor: High-contrast font color for clock and labels. * $textColorDanger: Error state indicator for incorrect password attempts. * $accentColorAttention: Warning color indicating Caps Lock activation.

docs.title: 2. Visual Elements & 4-Corner Architecture
docs.text:
Hyprlock uses Google Sans typography with automatic Nerd Font fallback for status icons, laid out in an ultra-clean 4-corner aesthetic:

[ 󰀉 Avatar ]                                              [ 󰤨   󰂯   󰂄 37% ]
(Top-Left)                                                    (Top-Right)

                               [ 21:54 ]
                         Wednesday, 21 October

                           [  Password  ]


[ 󰖑  9°  •  Bogota ]                                       [ 󰎆  Now Playing ]
(Bottom-Left)                                                 (Bottom-Right)

source = /home/zero/.config/themes/current/hyprlock.conf
$font = Google Sans

general {
  hide_cursor = true
  fail_timeout = 1000
}

# USER AVATAR (Top Left - Circular Badge)
image {
  monitor =
  path = /home/zero/.config/hypr/avatar.png
  size = 32
  rounding = -1
  border_size = 2
  border_color = $accentColorPurple
  position = 30, -26
  halign = left
  valign = top
}

# SYSTEM STATUS (Network, Bluetooth, Battery - Top Right)
label {
  monitor =

docs.title: 5. Auxiliary Scripts (~/dotfiles/hypr/scripts/)
docs.text:
All lockscreen scripts are optimized for zero-latency execution (< 2ms) without synchronous network blocking:

  • weather (~/.config/hypr/scripts/weather): Reads cached weather data (~/.cache/weather.json) generated by Quickshell, mapping WWO condition codes to Nerd Font glyphs (󰖙, 󰖕, 󰖐, 󰖗, 󰼲, 󰙾, 󰖑) and rendering 󰖑 9° • Bogota.

  • status (~/.config/hypr/scripts/status): Merges network, bluetooth, and battery into a single spaced string (󰤨 󰂯 󰂄 37%) to ensure pixel-perfect alignment.
  • network (~/.config/hypr/scripts/network): Non-blocking interface status check (/sys/class/net/*/operstate) displaying 󰈀 (Ethernet), 󰤨 (Wi-Fi), or 󰤭 (Disconnected).
  • bluetooth (~/.config/hypr/scripts/bluetooth): Instant radio status check via rfkill displaying 󰂯 (Active) or 󰂲 (Disabled).
  • battery (~/.config/hypr/scripts/battery): Fast capacity and AC status check via /sys/class/power_supply/.

docs.title: Hypridle Daemon Configuration
docs.text:
hypridle runs as a persistent background daemon launched from autostart.conf:

exec-once = hypridle

docs.title: Configuration (hypridle.conf)
docs.text:
general {
    before_sleep_cmd = hyprlock
    after_sleep_cmd = hyprctl dispatch dpms on
    ignore_dbus_inhibit = false
    lock_cmd = hyprlock
}

listener {
    timeout = 300
    on-timeout = hyprlock
}
  • Sleep Safeguard: before_sleep_cmd = hyprlock guarantees the session locks immediately before system suspend or hibernation.
  • Wake Recovery: after_sleep_cmd = hyprctl dispatch dpms on restores display power as soon as the system resumes.
  • Inactivity Rule: timeout = 300 automatically triggers hyprlock after 5 minutes of continuous user inactivity.

docs.title: How to Create and Add New Shaders
docs.text: Follow this quick step-by-step guide to create, register, and integrate a new shader into both Hyprland and the Quickshell UI.

docs.title: Step 1: Write the GLSL Fragment Shader
docs.text:
Create a new .glsl file in ~/.config/hypr/shaders/<shader-name>.glsl. Hyprland shaders use OpenGL ES 3.20 syntax:

#version 320 es
precision highp float;

in vec2 v_texcoord;
uniform sampler2D tex;
out vec4 fragColor;

void main() {
    vec4 pix = texture(tex, v_texcoord);
    vec3 col = pix.rgb;

    // Apply custom color transformations here
    // Example: Invert colors
    col = 1.0 - col;

    fragColor = vec4(col, pix.a);
}

docs.title: Step 2: Register the Shader in the Filter Script
docs.text:
Open ~/.config/hypr/scripts/filter and add a new case matching your shader name:

    myshader)
        apply_shader "My Custom Shader" "$SHADER_DIR/myshader.glsl"
        ;;

Update the usage message at the bottom of the script to include your new filter keyword.

docs.title: Step 3: Generate the Preview Thumbnail
docs.text:
Apply the shader and take a clean 480x300 px snapshot using hyprctl and grim:

# Apply your new shader
hyprctl keyword decoration:screen_shader "$HOME/.config/hypr/shaders/myshader.glsl"

# Capture and resize thumbnail
grim -o eDP-1 /tmp/raw_thumb.png
magick /tmp/raw_thumb.png -resize 480x300^ -gravity center -extent 480x300 "$HOME/.config/quickshell/assets/shaders/myshader.png"
rm -f /tmp/raw_thumb.png

docs.title: Step 4: Add the Entry to Quickshell Launcher
docs.text:
Open ~/.config/quickshell/modules/launcher/Launcher.qml and append your shader to the shadersList array:

{
    id: "myshader",
    name: "My Custom Shader",
    filterName: "My Custom Shader",
    desc: "Short visual summary of the effect",
    thumb: shaderThumbDir + "myshader.png"
}

docs.title: Step 5: Reload and Verify
docs.text:
Reload Quickshell to pick up the changes:

~/.config/quickshell/restart-quickshell.sh

Press SUPER + B to verify that your new shader card appears with its thumbnail, title, and description, and activates on click or Enter.

docs.title: XWayland Compatibility & Window Rules
docs.text: This document details the architectural challenges encountered when running legacy X11 and Chromium Embedded Framework (CEF) / Electron applications through XWayland on Hyprland, along with compositor rules to eliminate graphical artifacts, transparent boxes, and unwanted borders around popup windows.

docs.title: Background & Architecture
docs.text:
While most modern Wayland applications support native Wayland protocols (using subsurfaces, xdg-shell, and client-side popups), several popular applications still rely on XWayland:

  • Spotify: Uses a custom Chromium Embedded Framework (CEF) build that crashes when forced into native Wayland with GPU acceleration ([FATAL:content/browser/gpu/gpu_data_manager_impl_private.cc] GPU process isn't usable).
  • Steam: Relies on X11 libraries for window management and overlays.
  • Electron / Chromium legacy apps: Run under X11 by default unless explicitly configured with Ozone Wayland flags.

docs.title: The Issue: Transparent Popup Boxes & Shadow Artifacts
docs.text:
Under XWayland, dropdown menus, context menus, and tooltips are rendered by the client application inside an oversized rectangular X11 window surface. The application draws its own soft drop-shadow into the padding around the actual menu content.

Because XWayland passes the entire buffer to Hyprland as a flat surface without subsurface alpha metadata:

  1. Blur Bleed: When decoration:blur:popups = true is enabled in decoration.conf, Hyprland applies the compositor blur pass across the entire transparent buffer, producing a blurry, frosted rectangle around context menus.
  2. Double Shadows: Hyprland's decoration:shadow draws an outer window shadow around the bounding rectangle of the XWayland window, resulting in double shadows or dark rectangular borders.
  3. Unwanted Borders: Without explicit exclusion, popup menus may inherit the global border_size defined in general:border_size.
┌──────────────────────────────────────────────┐  <-- Hyprland bounding box (blurred & shadowed)
│      Transparent X11 Padding Buffer          │
│   ┌────────────────────────────────────┐     │
│   │   Actual Context / Dropdown Menu   │     │
│   │   • Item 1                         │     │
│   │   • Item 2                         │     │
│   └────────────────────────────────────┘     │
│                                              │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: The Fix: Hyprland Window Rules
docs.text:
Hyprland provides granular window rule properties (match:) to target XWayland popups specifically without degrading visual effects on main tiled or floating windows.

In ~/.config/hypr/window.conf:

# Prevent transparent box and blur artifacts on XWayland popups/dropdown menus
windowrule = no_blur on, match:xwayland 1, match:float 1, match:title ^$
windowrule = no_shadow on, match:xwayland 1, match:float 1, match:title ^$

docs.title: Breakdown of Match Properties
docs.text:
Property Value Description match:xwayland 1 Restricts the rule strictly to windows managed by the XWayland bridge. match:float 1 Matches only floating surfaces (dropdowns and context menus are always floating). match:title ^$ Matches empty window titles. In XWayland, dropdown menus and popups are spawned with an empty string title, distinguishing them from actual titled floating dialogs. no_blur on Effect Disables compositor background blur across the transparent buffer. no_shadow on Effect Disables Hyprland's external window shadow for the popup.

Eliminating Extraneous Borders

If an XWayland application creates menus with borders from Hyprland's general:border_size, append the following rule: 

windowrule = no_border on, match:xwayland 1, match:float 1, match:title ^$

docs.title: Native Wayland Alternative (When Supported)
docs.text: For applications that have working Wayland backends, running them natively eliminates the need for XWayland workarounds entirely:

docs.title: Google Chrome / Chromium
docs.text:
Add the following flags to ~/.config/chrome-flags.conf (or ~/.config/chromium-flags.conf):

--ozone-platform-hint=auto
--enable-features=WaylandWindowDecorations

docs.title: Electron Applications (VS Code, Discord, Obsidian)
docs.text:
Launch with standard Ozone arguments:

code --ozone-platform=wayland --enable-features=UseOzonePlatform

(Note: As verified in our testing, Spotify's bundled CEF cannot use these flags without crashing; Spotify should continue running via --ozone-platform=x11 with the window rules described above).

docs.title: Verification & Debugging
docs.text:
To inspect window properties and verify if a window is running under XWayland or native Wayland, run:

hyprctl clients

Look for the following fields in the output:

  • xwayland: 1 — The window is running under XWayland.
  • xwayland: 0 — The window is running natively on Wayland.
  • class and title — Use these values to refine your match: expressions.

docs.title: Quickshell & Control Center
docs.text: Quickshell is the Wayland-native QML widget framework driving this desktop environment. It provides a One UI inspired control center featuring translucent cards, rounded pill toggles, and reactive sliders on top of the Hyprland compositor.

docs.title: Modules Overview
docs.text:
• Control Center (modules/controlcenter/):
  • Dynamic Island Shelf Architecture: Docked directly below Waybar (shelfHeight: 36px, y: 0, anchors.rightMargin: 0) with a borderless glass surface (border.width: 0, alpha 0.80) matching the top status bar.
  • Concave Transition Fillet: Hardware-accelerated QtQuick.Shapes inverted fillet (28 px radius) bridging Waybar's horizontal bottom edge with the panel's left vertical shoulder, creating a continuous molded Dynamic Island appearance.
  • Instant & Clean Deployment: Completely eliminates overshoot bouncing and clipped vertical resizing for instantaneous, responsive activation.
  • Layout Architecture: Balanced two-column grid layout featuring a left widgets column (Analog Clock, Weather, Media Player) and a right control matrix (4x3 quick toggle grid alongside vertical glassmorphic sliders).
  • Analog Clock Widget (AnalogClockWidget.qml): Canvas-based analog dial with dynamic hour and minute hands, digital time readout, and localized English weekday and calendar date.
  • Weather Widget (WeatherWidget.qml): Live atmospheric conditions, ambient temperature, location label, and relative humidity fetched via OpenWeather API in English.
  • Vertical Sliders Card: Frosted glassmorphic card housing vertical reactive sliders for PipeWire audio volume and brightnessctl display backlight.
  • Quick Toggles (4x3 Grid): Rounded pill buttons for Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, DND, Airplane Mode, Caffeine, Power Profiles, Night Light, Screen Shaders, Audio outputs, Dynamic Theming, Energy, and Wallpaper selection.
  • Orbital Radar Submenus (WifiSection.qml, BluetoothSection.qml):
    • Wi-Fi Orbital Radar: Central localhost host node with discovered networks revolving in concentric orbits. Orbital radius is dynamically mapped to signal strength (stronger signal orbits closer to the host). Features a fixed right-side telemetry card displaying active connection metrics (SSID, security protocol, local IP/CIDR, live dBm and transfer rates), fast instant caching, and a pause/resume animation button with state persisted in radar_preferences.json.
    • Bluetooth Orbital Radar: Central host node with paired and discovered devices in dynamic orbital paths. Includes an interactive device iconography picker (Nerd Font glyphs for mouse, keyboard, headphones, speaker, gamepad, and generic device) with persistent mapping in bluetooth_icons.json, fixed right-side connection telemetry card, and an independent pause/resume toggle.
  • Energy & Performance Dashboard (BatterySection.qml): Dedicated hardware metrics subpage displaying charge percentage, discharge rates, full charge estimates, battery health state, power draw, charge cycles, and power profile presets (Power Saver, Balanced, Performance).
  • Waybar Sync: Seamless bidirectional state sync between quick toggles (Caffeine, Night Light, Shader, Power Profiles) and top status bar indicators using POSIX signals (including SIGRTMIN+11 for instantaneous power profile updates).
  • Notifications & Dynamic Island Toasts (modules/controlcenter/, modules/notifications/):
  • Native DBus notification server (org.freedesktop.Notifications) managed by NotificationService.qml.
  • Top-center Dynamic Island toast layer (NotificationToastLayer.qml) docked flush with Waybar (shelfHeight: 36px), featuring dual concave transition fillets (28 px radius), flat top edges, and downward slide emergence animation.
  • Collapsible notifications card embedded directly inside the Control Center featuring the title Notifications • ( # ), rotating toggle chevron, quick "Clear all" action, empty placeholder state, and scrollable notification list.
  • Waybar notification bell triggers qs ipc call notifications toggle, opening the Control Center with the notifications card smoothly expanded.
  • Full design parameters and easing curves detailed in the Notifications & OSDs Guide.
  • Clipboard Manager (modules/clipboard/):
  • Dynamic Island Shelf Architecture: Docked flush below Waybar (shelfHeight: 36px, y: 0, anchors.rightMargin: 0) with seamless 28 px concave transition fillet and continuous 2 px accent outline (Root.Theme.primary).
  • Compact Geometry: Scaled to 616 px width (30% narrower than the standard 880 px panel) for clean, unobtrusive clipboard history management.
  • Unified Translucency: Panel background with 0.85 opacity (Root.Theme.panelBg) and cards styled at 0.95 opacity (Root.Theme.surfaceContainer) matching the Notification Center design system.
  • Functionality: Real-time text history populated via cliphist list, instant re-copying via cliphist decode <id> | wl-copy, and quick pill button for wiping history.
  • Triggering: Accessible via Waybar quick action button or globally using SUPER + V (qs ipc call clipboard toggle). Detailed in the Clipboard Manager Guide.
  • DeskClock & Calendar (modules/deskclock/, modules/calendar/):
  • Ambient desktop clock surface and expandable calendar panel with date navigation.
  • Unified Music Player (modules/launcher/):
  • Bottom-docked non-modal interactive MPRIS music controller integrated inside the launcher. Triggered globally with SUPER + M (qs ipc call miniplayer toggle) or by typing /music, featuring passthrough desktop click masking and full playback controls.
  • Application Launcher & Dynamic Island Carousel (modules/launcher/):
  • Bottom-docked runner (anchors.bottomMargin: 0) with dual concave fillets (28 px radius) seamlessly emerging from the screen's bottom bezel.
  • Powers Application Drawer, Wallpaper Carousel, Shader Selector, Theme Carousel, and Gadget Manager. Detailed in the Launcher & Wallpapers Guide.
  • Workspace Overview & Exposé (modules/overview/):
  • Full-screen 2x5 grid displaying all 10 Hyprland workspaces simultaneously with proportional window layouts.
  • Drag-and-drop window relocation across workspaces, quick window kill, and spatial keyboard navigation.
  • Triggered globally with SUPER + Tab / SUPER + SHIFT + Tab. Detailed in the Workspace Overview Guide.
  • Keyboard Shortcuts Overlay (modules/shortcuts/):
  • Wayland-native cheat sheet modal triggered via F1 featuring live search, category pills, two-column card grid, and glassmorphic styling aligned with the Control Center. Detailed in the Keyboard Shortcuts Guide.

docs.text: The Clipboard Manager (quickshell:clipboard) is a Wayland-native history drawer built directly into Quickshell. Docked smoothly below the Waybar Status Bar and integrated with cliphist, it provides an instantaneous, visual clipboard buffer for text and image previews.

docs.title: Architecture & Visual Design
docs.text:
The module (modules/clipboard/ClipboardPanel.qml and ClipboardItem.qml) adheres strictly to the Dynamic Island and Material Design 3 aesthetics established across the desktop environment:

  • Dynamic Island Shelf Architecture: Docked flush below Waybar (shelfHeight: 36px, y: 0, anchors.rightMargin: 0) on the top-right edge of the active display.

docs.title: 1. High-Performance Controller (clipboard-manager.py)
docs.text:
Backend operations are managed by a dedicated, asynchronous Python controller (~/.config/quickshell/scripts/clipboard-manager.py) outputting structured JSON to Quickshell's quickshell.io.Process pipelines:

  • Buffer & Streaming: Reads real-time entries from cliphist list, streaming up to 50 active items directly to the QML model.
  • Binary Detection: Automatically identifies PNG, JPEG, and GIF binary streams or [[ binary data ]] descriptors without blocking the UI thread.
  • Thumbnail Cache: Decodes image entries on demand into /tmp/cliphist-thumbs/<id>.png with zero redundant re-decoding.
  • Surgical Deletion: Targets exact entry lines for deletion using cliphist delete and cleans up associated cached thumbnails.

docs.title: 2. Live Search & Instant Filtering
docs.text:
• Debounced Search Bar: Clean search input field located below the header with real-time text matching (140 ms debounce) over entry previews.
  • Quick Reset: One-click clear button (✕) to instantly restore the full 50-item catalog.
  • Dynamic Placeholders: Responsive empty states differentiating between an empty clipboard and zero search query matches.

docs.title: 3. Multimedia & Screenshot Previews
docs.text:
• Image Thumbnails: Captured screenshots and copied images render a dedicated 90x68 px preview container (Image.PreserveAspectFit) with rounded corners and dark contrast backing.
  • Format & Dimensions Telemetry: Displays dimensions metadata (e.g., 1920x1080) when available from cliphist.
  • Binary Re-Injection: Clicking an image card re-injects the exact original binary payload back into the Wayland clipboard via cliphist decode <id> | wl-copy.

docs.title: 4. Interactive Feedback & Per-Item Deletion
docs.text:
• Copied Feedback (✓): Clicking any card triggers an instant checkmark badge and an accent outline pulse, providing immediate visual confirmation before dismissal.
  • Single-Item Deletion (✕): Hovering over any card exposes a dedicated circular delete button. Clicking it removes only that specific item via cliphist delete, allowing sensitive data (such as passwords or tokens) to be purged without wiping the entire history.
  • Unified Clear Action: Bottom-aligned pill button ("Clear all") styled with error-accented hover reactions to wipe all stored entries via cliphist wipe.

docs.title: 1. Borderless & Containerless Visual Philosophy
docs.text: Unlike traditional desktop widgets that wrap content inside heavy translucent glass cards, drop shadows, or bounding borders, Quickshell Desktop Gadgets are completely borderless and containerless. Typography, icons, and progress meters float directly over the desktop background. This minimalist design ensures that your wallpaper remains the focal point while ambient information stays legible and unobtrusive.

docs.title: 2. Fullscreen Bottom Layer (WlrLayer.Bottom)
docs.text: Each gadget is hosted inside an individual PanelWindow configured with: * WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Bottom: The window renders directly above the desktop wallpaper (WlrLayer.Background) but strictly below regular application windows (WlrLayer.Top and normal Wayland surfaces). Application windows tile and float across gadgets without any z-order interference. * exclusionMode: ExclusionMode.Ignore: Informs the compositor (Hyprland) that gadgets do not reserve screen space. They cause zero window layout displacement, never compressing your tiling columns or shifting panels like Waybar. * WlrLayershell.keyboardFocus: WlrKeyboardFocus.None: The layer shell surface does not trap global keyboard focus, ensuring normal shortcuts continue to function without interruption.

docs.title: 3. Dynamic Wayland Input Masking (mask: Region)
docs.text:
In Wayland Layer Shell, a transparent fullscreen surface would normally capture all mouse input, blocking clicks to desktop icons, wallpaper menus, or underlying windows.

To resolve this, every gadget employs dynamic input masking:

mask: Region {
    item: mainCard
}

The compositor restricts hit-testing strictly to the bounding geometry of mainCard. Any mouse click outside the active card passes directly through to the desktop background or the window underneath.

docs.title: 4. Direct Native Drag ("Drag Anywhere")
docs.text:
Conventional Wayland floating widgets often suffer from severe cursor jitter or rubber-banding during mouse dragging, caused by round-trip latency between client-side drag events and compositor surface repositioning requests.

Quickshell eliminates this bottleneck through a Direct Native Drag design: 1. The PanelWindow stays anchored fullscreen (top, bottom, left, right: true). 2. Inside the window, mainCard uses Qt Quick's hardware-accelerated MouseArea: 

MouseArea {
    id: dragArea
    anchors.fill: parent
    cursorShape: pressed ? Qt.ClosedHandCursor : (containsMouse ? Qt.OpenHandCursor : Qt.ArrowCursor)
    drag.target: mainCard
    drag.axis: Drag.XAndYAxis
    onPressed: mainCard.isDragging = true
    onReleased: {
        var fx = Math.round(mainCard.x)
        var fy = Math.round(mainCard.y)
        Root.GadgetsManager.setPosition("gadgetId", fx, fy)
        mainCard.isDragging = false
    }
}
3. Moving the gadget executes locally on the GPU at your monitor's native refresh rate (144Hz, 165Hz, or 240Hz) with zero compositor round-trips. 4. When released, integer coordinates (Math.round) are committed to GadgetsManager.qml and saved to disk.

docs.title: 5. Discrete Hover Controls
docs.text: Gadgets do not render permanent title bars or close icons. Instead, moving the mouse over the gadget card smoothly reveals contextual controls via an animated opacity transition (NumberAnimation { duration: 180 }): * Close Button (✕): Positioned in the upper-right corner. Clicking it invokes GadgetsManager.setEnabled(id, false), hiding the gadget instantly and updating persistent storage. * Action Icons: Gadgets like Daily Spark reveal interactive cycling buttons (󰑐) only when hovered.

docs.title: Troubleshooting & Maintenance
docs.text:
How do I reset all gadgets to their default positions?

To restore factory coordinate positions, stop Quickshell and delete or reset the configuration file: 

killall quickshell
rm ~/.config/quickshell/gadgets.json
quickshell &
Quickshell will regenerate gadgets.json with standard balanced coordinates.

A gadget does not respond to clicks outside its card

This indicates that Wayland input masking is working properly. The transparent fullscreen window deliberately passes all clicks through to your wallpaper or underlying windows. Clicks are only captured directly on the widget's content area (mask: Region { item: mainCard }).

Weather widget displays 'Loading...' or fallback data

Verify internet connectivity and test the backend script manually in your terminal: 

python3 ~/.config/quickshell/scripts/weather.py
If wttr.in is temporarily rate-limited, ensure ~/.cache/weather.json is writable. You can optionally export your OpenWeatherMap key in ~/.config/weather/api_key and city in ~/.config/weather/city.

Hardware Pulse CPU temperature reads 0°C

Check your Linux thermal zone permissions: 

ls -l /sys/class/thermal/thermal_zone*/temp
On custom kernels or non-standard hardware, verify which thermal zone corresponds to your CPU package and ensure unprivileged read access is permitted.

docs.title: Floating Launcher & Animated Wallpaper Carousel
docs.text: Quickshell implements a floating bottom-center application launcher and animated wallpaper selector inspired by Caelestia Shell. The component is integrated directly with Wayland layershell, Matugen color extraction, and hardware-accelerated QML transitions.

docs.title: Architecture Overview
docs.text:
The system consists of two coordinated Quickshell modules:

  1. Floating Launcher & Dynamic Island Drawer (modules/launcher/):
  2. Placed on WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Overlay.
  3. Horizontally centered and docked directly to the bottom edge of the display (anchors.bottomMargin: 0).
  4. Dynamic Island emergence geometry: top corners rounded (topLeftRadius: 28, topRightRadius: 28), bottom corners square (bottomLeftRadius: 0, bottomRightRadius: 0), and borderless glass finish matching Waybar (alpha 0.80).
  5. Hardware-accelerated dual concave fillets (QtQuick.Shapes with 28 px radius) smoothly bridging the bottom screen edge into both vertical shoulders of the card.
  6. Search input at the bottom with real-time mode detection:
    • Application Mode (default): Lists system desktop entries with official icons, titles, and descriptions.
    • Command / Actions Mode (/ or >): Activated by typing / (or >) to expose system commands.
    • Wallpaper Carousel (/wallpaper / SUPER + W): Horizontal card carousel featuring 16:9 previews, active wallpaper glow, and a local file explorer.
    • Shader Selector (/shader): Real-time hyprland post-processing screen shader carousel.
    • Theme Carousel (/theme): Material Design 3 and custom theme palette selector.
    • Gadget Manager (/gadgets): Ambient desktop widgets toggler.
    • Music Player Mode (/music / SUPER + M): Bottom-docked MPRIS controller with non-modal desktop click passthrough.
  7. Desktop Background Engine (modules/background/Background.qml):
  8. Placed on WlrLayershell.layer: WlrLayer.Background on all connected displays (Quickshell.screens).
  9. Implements a double-buffer (ping-pong) layer switching architecture, guaranteeing reliable consecutive wallpaper transitions without QML property binding degradation.
  10. Manages smooth cross-image animations, replacing static background setters like swaybg.
  11. Applies the "Zoom & Blur" (Emergence) transition:
    • Outgoing wallpaper scales from 1.0 to 1.15 while fading opacity from 1.0 to 0.0 in 750 ms (Easing.InOutQuad).
    • Incoming wallpaper scales from 0.88 to 1.0 while fading opacity from 0.0 to 1.0 in 750 ms (Easing.InOutQuad).
  12. Triggers apply-matugen.sh asynchronously only when matugen was previously selected, preserving active manual themes upon wallpaper transitions.

docs.title: 1. Application Search Mode
docs.text: When the search input is empty or contains standard text: * Lists all installed .desktop applications discovered by list-apps.py. * Shows application icon, title in bold, and comment / category description. * High-Contrast Selection Feedback: * Active item receives a vibrant translucent primary tint (rgba(primary, 0.22)) and 1.5 px glowing primary border. * Vertical accent pill indicator on the left border. * Prominent [ 󰌑 Enter ] badge on the right edge. * Dynamic icon and title scale expansion. * Keyboard navigation: Up / Down arrows move selection with automatic viewport positioning (positionViewAtIndex), Enter executes the application and closes the launcher, Escape cancels.

docs.title: 2. Action / Command Mode (/ or >)
docs.text: Typing / (or >) filters available system commands: * Wallpaper Carousel: Enters the horizontal wallpaper picker carousel (/wallpaper). * Theme Carousel: Enters the horizontal visual theme picker carousel (/theme). * Lock Screen: Locks session using hyprlock. * Sleep / Suspend: Suspends the machine to RAM (systemctl suspend). * Restart System / Shut Down: Session reboot and power-off actions.

docs.title: 3. Wallpaper Carousel Mode
docs.text: Typing /wallpaper (or pressing SUPER + W) opens the horizontal carousel: * Expanded floating card container (1080 px width, 340 px height, 24 px radius) offering generous horizontal and vertical headroom. * Caelestia Shell Containment & Edge Fade Overlays: * Strict clipping (clip: true) enforced across the floating dock card, content viewport, and horizontal list view, eliminating lateral overflow beyond container boundaries. * Left and right 32 px horizontal gradient fade overlays that smoothly blend scrollable cards into the dark dock background without hard cutoffs. * Displays 16:9 cards (224x214 px with 120 px thumbnail height) generated from /home/zero/Pictures/walls/ and cached in ~/.cache/wallpapers/. * Hover & Selection Styling: * Dynamic elevation: Cards lift upward by -5 px on hover (-2 px on keyboard selection). * Smooth scale: Subtle 1.05 expansion on hover (1.03 on keyboard selection) with Easing.OutCubic. * Internal thumbnail zoom: 16:9 thumbnail expands to 1.05 within rounded bounds. * Vibrant halo glow: Border widens to 2 px with primary accent color and expanded glow margins. * Active Badge: The currently active desktop wallpaper is highlighted with an "Active" badge and a focused double border. * Add Local File Card: Positioned at the end of the carousel. Clicking or pressing Enter opens a native file dialog (zenity) to import external images, automatically caching thumbnails and applying the wallpaper.

docs.title: 4. Theme Carousel Mode
docs.text: Typing /theme or /tema (also >theme), clicking "Theme" in the Control Center, or executing qs ipc call launcher theme opens the horizontal theme carousel: * Reuses the same 1080 px floating container (smoothly expanding from 340 px to 392 px height when Matugen or Custom is selected) and horizontal scroll architecture as the wallpaper carousel. * Featured Themes Order: * 1. Wallpaper (Matugen): Dynamic Material Design 3 generation based on active wallpaper. * 2. Custom Accent: Fixed deep onyx black surfaces (#0A0A0C) with interactive accent color chip selector. * Static Presets: Cobalt Night, Amethyst, Arctic Mist, Crimson Night, and Cyberpunk. * Matugen Dynamic Modes Selector: * When "Wallpaper (Matugen)" is selected or active, an animated top header gracefully expands with Material You mode pills for all 9 Matugen color scheme algorithms: Vibrant, Fruit Salad, Monochrome, Tonal Spot, Expressive, Rainbow, Fidelity, Content, and Neutral. * Live Palette Preview: Clicking any mode chip immediately applies that scheme via apply-matugen.sh in the background, updating desktop accent colors and Quickshell in real-time without dismissing the launcher. * The active scheme type is saved to ~/.config/themes/current/scheme_type and preserved across subsequent wallpaper transitions. * Custom Accent Color Bar: * When "Custom" is selected, an animated top bar expands with interactive color pills (Carmesí, Lava, Ámbar, Esmeralda, Turquesa, Cyan, Cobalto, Amatista, Fucsia, Rosa). * Clicking any accent immediately updates Quickshell, saves the preference to ~/.config/quickshell/custom-accent, and executes apply-theme.sh custom across Waybar, Hyprland borders, Kitty, and Alacritty in real-time. * Visual Theme Cards (ThemeCard.qml): * Displays 224x214 px cards with a dedicated 120 px preview container showcasing an interface mockup for each palette. * Preview includes a miniature header, active primary widget, slider with active track, accent chip, and 5 color swatches (primary, primaryContainer, surfaceContainerHigh, connected, textPrimary). * Palette colors resolve via explicit Qt.color conversion, ensuring accurate rendering across static palettes, dynamic Custom accents, and Matugen extractions. * An "Active" badge dynamically marks the currently applied theme. * Interactive Behavior: * Selecting a card applies the theme instantly via Theme.currentTheme, persists it to ~/.config/quickshell/current-theme, and triggers apply-theme.sh or apply-matugen.sh across the system without abruptly closing the launcher, allowing live visual exploration until dismissed via Escape or clicking outside. * Full keyboard support with Left / Right navigation, Enter to apply, and text filtering (e.g. >theme cobalt).

docs.title: 5. Desktop Gadgets Mode (/gadgets or /widgets)
docs.text: Typing /gadgets, /widgets, or /gadget (also with >), selecting "Desktop Gadgets" from the / commands list, or running qs ipc call launcher gadgets opens the desktop gadgets carousel: * Interactive Gadget Cards (GadgetCard.qml): * Displays 224x214 px cards showcasing live visual mockups of desktop widgets (DeskClock, Calendar, and future extensions). * Top-right badge dynamically indicates status: green Active checkmark or muted Hidden badge. * Clicking any card or pressing Enter toggles the gadget visibility on the desktop in real time. * On-Desktop Interaction & Architecture: * Zero-Container Transparency: Desktop gadgets float seamlessly with zero backgrounds, zero borders, and zero glow rectangles directly over the wallpaper. * Direct Native Drag ("Drag Anywhere"): Desktop gadgets use native Qt Quick drag.target hosted inside fullscreen WlrLayer.Bottom panels with dynamic input masking (mask: Region { item: mainCard }). Users can grab and drag the widget smoothly from anywhere on its surface at native monitor refresh rates with zero latency or rubber-banding. * Discrete Hover Close Button (✕): A minimalist close button appears on hover in the top-right corner to hide the gadget and persist its state. The gadget can be restored at any time via the /gadgets launcher carousel.

docs.title: 6. Unified Music Player Mode (/music)
docs.text: Typing /music, /musica, >music, or pressing SUPER + M (qs ipc call miniplayer toggle) opens the unified bottom-docked music player: * Non-Modal Passthrough Surface: * Disables modal screen dimming (dimBg.visible: false). * Relinquishes keyboard focus grabs (WlrKeyboardFocus.None), allowing full desktop interaction while music is open. * Masks mouse pointer events strictly to the active player card and its bottom fillets via mask: Region { item: musicRegionItem }, ensuring all transparent desktop areas pass clicks directly to background windows. * Full MPRIS Controls: * 140x140 px album art with hover focus overlay (clicking raises or launches the player application using focus-player.sh). * Track title and artist / identity labels with text truncation. * Interactive seekable progress bar with real-time position polling and mm:ss timestamp indicators. * Previous, Play/Pause toggle, and Next playback controls. * Explicit close button (✕) in the player header and search bar.

docs.title: IPC Commands and Keybindings
docs.text:
The launcher and background engine expose IPC endpoints:

# Toggle application launcher
qs ipc call launcher toggle

# Open unified music player directly
qs ipc call launcher music
qs ipc call miniplayer toggle

# Open wallpaper carousel directly
qs ipc call launcher wallpaper

# Open theme carousel directly
qs ipc call launcher theme
qs ipc call themepicker toggle

# Open desktop gadgets carousel directly
qs ipc call launcher gadgets

# Toggle individual gadgets via IPC
qs ipc call gadgets toggle deskclock
qs ipc call gadgets toggle calendar

# Navigate selection via IPC
qs ipc call launcher next
qs ipc call launcher prev
qs ipc call launcher activate

# Filter commands or text via IPC
qs ipc call launcher search ">"
qs ipc call launcher search "/gadgets"

# Set wallpaper programmatically with animated transition
qs ipc call wallpaper set "/path/to/image.png"

# Close the launcher (the same command reopens it)
qs ipc call launcher toggle

Note: hide() works over IPC, but qs ipc call <target> show is not dispatchable in Quickshell 0.3.1: the CLI prints the target's function list and the panel stays closed (reproduced on launcher, clipboard and controlcenter). Use toggle to open and close a panel, or qs ipc call launcher search "<query>", which always sets the launcher visible.

  • SUPER + W: Invokes qs ipc call launcher wallpaper to present the wallpaper carousel.

docs.title: Notifications & OSDs
docs.text: This guide details the architecture, screen positioning, and animation dynamics for floating notification toasts and on-screen display (OSD) cards (Volume, Brightness, and Song Transition OSD) in Quickshell running on the Hyprland compositor.

docs.title: Design Parameters and Dynamics
docs.text:
All floating indicators follow a standardized behavioral contract:

  1. Dynamic Island Integration with Waybar:
  2. Placement: Anchored to the top of the screen and centered horizontally (anchors.top: true, anchors.horizontalCenter: parent.horizontalCenter).
  3. Top Anchor: Directly docked beneath Waybar (topMargin: Root.Theme.shelfHeight, 36 px) with zero dead space.
  4. Unified Shape & Continuous Accent Border: Integrated into a unified QtQuick.Shapes geometry (layer.enabled: true, 4x multi-sampling) combining both 28 px concave shoulder fillets and the body into a seamless canvas. A continuous 2 px accent border (strokeWidth: 2, strokeColor: Root.Theme.primary, or Root.Theme.error on critical urgency) traces the left concave arc, down the flank, across the rounded base, and up the right concave arc while remaining cleanly open along the Waybar interface.
  5. Corner Radii: Square top edge matching Waybar's bottom shelf and generously rounded bottom corners (radius: 28).
  6. Surface Finish: Clean obsidian glass surface with exact opacity and color parity (Qt.rgba(panelBg.r, panelBg.g, panelBg.b, 0.85)). The top toast, Control Center, and media panels share this unified continuous border without interior seam lines or hover overlays.
  7. Theming: Colors, translucency, and accents are rendered dynamically using Matugen Dynamic Palette Tokens (_shelfBgColor, primary, textPrimary, textSecondary).
  8. Entrance Animation (Emergence from Waybar):
  9. Encapsulated within a clipped viewport (clip: true) so notifications physically slide out from beneath Waybar.
  10. Translates from _slideY: -height to 0 over 280 ms using Easing.OutCubic acceleration.
  11. Fades in opacity from 0 to 1 over 200 ms using Easing.OutQuad.
  12. Queue Dynamics: When a new notification arrives, it prepends to the stack (insert(0)) and fluidly pushes older active notifications downward using move: Transition.
  13. Dismissal Animation: Gently moves upward (to: -height) and fades out (opacity: 0) before unmounting from the model.
  14. LayerShell Surface Lifecycle & Input Masking:
  15. Dynamic Loader Lifecycle: The PanelWindow is instantiated via a Loader { active: toastModel.count > 0 }. When no toasts are active, the surface is completely unmapped from the Wayland compositor, eliminating stale layer surfaces.
  16. Targeted Surface Dimensions: Anchored at anchors.top: true with implicitWidth: 440 and dynamic height (Math.min(700, Root.Theme.shelfHeight + toastCol.implicitHeight + 40)).
  17. Layer Top: Placed on WlrLayer.Top, preventing pointer grabs and focus disruption on normal desktop windows.
  18. Input Masking: Uses mask: Region { item: toastWrapper } to restrict mouse interaction strictly to active notification cards and their concave fillets. All surrounding monitor areas pass pointer events directly through to underlying windows.

docs.title: Workspace Overview & Window Switcher
docs.text: The Workspace Overview (quickshell:overview) is a Wayland-native, hardware-accelerated full-screen desktop exposé and window management modal built directly into Quickshell. Triggered globally via SUPER + Tab, it displays a 2×5 responsive grid representing all 10 Hyprland workspaces, accurately rendering window placements, and enabling drag-and-drop window relocation across workspaces.

docs.title: Architecture & Visual Overview
docs.text:
flowchart TD
    Trigger["Hotkey: SUPER + Tab"] -->|IPC Dispatch| IPCHandler["Quickshell IpcHandler (overview)"]
    IPCHandler -->|Spawn Data Process| PythonScript["overview-data.py"]

    subgraph Data Pipeline
        PythonScript -->|Query| HyprMonitors["hyprctl -j monitors"]
        PythonScript -->|Query| HyprWorkspaces["hyprctl -j workspaces"]
        PythonScript -->|Query| HyprClients["hyprctl -j clients"]
        PythonScript -->|Map Icons| DesktopEntries["Desktop Entries (.desktop)"]
        HyprMonitors & HyprWorkspaces & HyprClients & DesktopEntries --> NormalizedJSON["Normalized 10-Workspace Geometry JSON"]
    end

    NormalizedJSON -->|Parse into Model| OverviewUI["Overview.qml (2x5 Grid)"]

    subgraph Interactive Controls
        OverviewUI -->|Tab / Arrows| CycleSelection["Sequential & Spatial Navigation"]
        OverviewUI -->|Enter / Click| FocusWin["hyprctl dispatch focuswindow"]
        OverviewUI -->|Drag & Drop| MoveWin["hyprctl dispatch movetoworkspacesilent"]
        OverviewUI -->|Click ✕ / Delete| CloseWin["hyprctl dispatch closewindow"]
    end

docs.title: File Structure
docs.text:
quickshell/
├── modules/
│   └── overview/
│       └── Overview.qml             # Full-screen 2x5 grid modal and drag-and-drop manager
├── scripts/
│   └── overview-data.py             # 6ms Hyprland geometry normalizer & app icon resolver
└── shell.qml                        # Mutual exclusivity coordinator & IPC target registration

docs.title: Design Specifications
docs.text:
• Surface Layout: 2 rows of 5 columns displaying all 10 workspaces simultaneously:
  • Top Row: Workspaces 1, 2, 3, 4, 5
  • Bottom Row: Workspaces 6, 7, 8, 9, 10
  • Aspect Ratio Preservation: Cards maintain the exact aspect ratio of the primary display (e.g. 16:10 for 1920×1200 or 16:9 for 1920×1080).
  • Workspace Numbering: Prominent 22 px bold numeral positioned in the top-right corner of each card with a high-contrast outline, illuminated with Theme.primary when active or selected.
  • Proportional Scaling Mathematics: $$\text{rel_x} = \text{at}[0] - \text{monitor.x}, \quad \text{rel_y} = \text{at}[1] - \text{monitor.y}$$ $$\text{norm_x} = \frac{\text{rel_x}}{\text{monitor.width}}, \quad \text{norm_y} = \frac{\text{rel_y}}{\text{monitor.height}}$$ Each window inside the card is placed at: $$x = \text{norm_x} \times \text{card.width}, \quad y = \text{norm_y} \times \text{card.height}$$
  • Minimum Window Enclosure: Clamped to a minimum of 48×32 px to prevent sub-pixel collapse on heavily tiled windows, guaranteeing icon and title visibility.
  • Miniature Desktop Wallpaper: Automatically renders the current desktop wallpaper (~/.config/themes/current/wallpaper) with an ambient darkened scrim behind each workspace canvas.
  • Zero Overhead Idle: The overlay component is wrapped in a lazy Loader { active: overviewScope.visible }. When dismissed, all QML elements and processes are destroyed, using 0% CPU and 0 MB RAM.

docs.title: 1. Drag & Drop Window Relocation
docs.text:
Windows can be dragged directly between any of the 10 workspaces in plain sight:

  1. Drag Initiation: Clicking and dragging any window card beyond an 8 px deadzone activates drag mode.
  2. Elevated Drag Ghost: A floating card (135×44 px) follows the mouse cursor with a 95% opacity acrylic surface, the application's system icon, and live target text ("Move to WS X").
  3. Workspace Hit-Testing: A high-frequency timer tracks global cursor coordinates mapped into local canvas space (mapFromItem), dynamically highlighting candidate drop targets in connected accent green (Theme.connected).
  4. Silent Relocation Dispatch: Upon release over a different workspace: 
    hyprctl dispatch movetoworkspacesilent <target_ws>,address:<window_address>
    The compositor transfers the window silently without shifting the user's viewport, and the overview refreshes immediately.

docs.title: 2. Window Management & Identity
docs.text:
• Desktop Icon Resolution: overview-data.py inspects /usr/share/applications, ~/.local/share/applications, and Flatpak export paths, pairing WM class names (kitty, zen, Shortwave) with system icon names fed to Quickshell.iconPath().
  • Quick Close Button: Hovering over any window reveals a ✕ close button in the mini-titlebar, invoking hyprctl dispatch closewindow address:<addr>.
  • Selected Window Inspector: A bottom pill displays the focused application icon, app name, full window title, and active keyboard shortcuts.

docs.title: 3. Keyboard & Mouse Controls
docs.text: Input Action SUPER + Tab / Tab Open overview / Cycle to next window across workspaces SUPER + SHIFT + Tab / Shift + Tab Cycle to previous window Arrow Keys (←, →) Move selection across adjacent workspaces Arrow Keys (↑, ↓) Spatial 2D grid jump (moves ±5 workspaces between rows) 1 – 9, 0 Instant jump to workspace 1–10 Enter / Space Focus selected window and close overview Delete / Backspace Close selected window Esc / Click Outside Close overview without changing focus Click Window Focus that window directly Click Workspace Canvas Switch directly to that workspace Drag & Drop Window Relocate window to target workspace

docs.title: Mutual Exclusivity
docs.text:
The module coordinates with Quickshell's other floating overlays:

  • Opening the Overview automatically dismisses the Power Menu, Control Center, App Launcher, and Clipboard Panel.
  • Opening any other overlay immediately closes the Overview modal.

docs.title: IPC Interface
docs.text:
The module registers under IPC target overview:

# Toggle visibility
quickshell ipc call overview toggle

# Open and focus next window
quickshell ipc call overview next

# Open and focus previous window
quickshell ipc call overview prev

# Close overview
quickshell ipc call overview close

docs.title: Keyboard Shortcuts Overlay
docs.text: The Shortcuts Overlay (quickshell:shortcuts) is a Wayland-native cheat sheet modal built into Quickshell. Triggered globally via F1, it provides an interactive, searchable reference of all active Hyprland keybindings and system actions.

docs.title: Architecture & Visual Design
docs.text:
The module (modules/shortcuts/ShortcutsOverlay.qml) aligns with the One UI and Material Design 3 aesthetic established in the Control Center:

  • Surface Geometry: Centered modal container measuring 920x660 px with a 28 px corner radius (Root.Theme.panelRadius).
  • Glassmorphic Finish: Translucent dark glass surface (Qt.rgba(surface.r, surface.g, surface.b, 0.78)) backed by hardware-accelerated Hyprland blur (layerrule = blur on, ignore_alpha 0, match:namespace quickshell:.*) and an outline border (1.5 px).
  • Backdrop Layer: Full-screen darkened scrim (Qt.rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.45)) that dismisses the overlay on click.
  • Responsive 2-Column Grid: Two-column card flow providing ample horizontal width for long descriptions and multi-key sequences.
  • Keycap Chip Rendering: Key combinations are split into distinct rounded keycaps (e.g., SUPER, SHIFT, R) styled with primary accent tones and high-contrast labels.

docs.title: 1. Dynamic Keybind Parser
docs.text:
The overlay reads ~/.config/hypr/binds.conf directly via a background quickshell.io.Process stream. Rather than dumping raw compositor dispatchers, the parser:

  • Resolves Hyprland variable references ($mainMod, $terminal, $fileManager, $menu).
  • Normalizes modifier combinations and translates hardware keys (Return to Enter, Print to Print Screen, audio and brightness XF86 symbols).
  • Groups repetitive workspace transitions (workspace 1..10, movetoworkspace 1..10) and directional focus arrows into concise entries.
  • Maps binds into categorized sets: Applications, Windows, Workspaces, and System & Media.

docs.title: 2. Live Search and Category Filtering
docs.text:
• Real-time Filter: Live search bar filtering instantly across key names, dispatchers, and localized descriptions.
  • Category Pills: Quick-switch filter buttons:
  • All (all): Complete catalog of user and desktop actions.
  • Applications (apps): Terminal, file manager, app launcher, wallpaper selector, and utility launchers.
  • Windows (windows): Window kill, floating toggle, fullscreen, focus navigation, and mouse drag/resize.
  • Workspaces (workspaces): Workspace navigation and window routing.
  • System (system): Audio volume, monitor brightness, screenshots, screen recording, OCR, and GLSL shaders.

docs.title: 3. LayerShell and Navigation
docs.text:
• Namespace: quickshell:shortcuts
  • Layer: WlrLayer.Overlay with WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive
  • Dismissal Actions:
  • Pressing F1 or Escape (handled by declarative QML Shortcut components).
  • Clicking the dedicated top-right circular close button.
  • Clicking the dark outer scrim.

docs.title: IPC Interface
docs.text:
The overlay exposes an IPC target callable from Hyprland keybindings or terminal scripts:

# Toggle visibility (mapped to F1 in ~/.config/hypr/binds.conf)
quickshell ipc call shortcuts toggle

# Open explicitly
quickshell ipc call shortcuts open

# Close explicitly
quickshell ipc call shortcuts close

docs.title: Alacritty Configuration
docs.text: Alacritty serves as the secondary terminal emulator in this environment, running the Zsh Shell with instant live configuration reloading and tight integration with the Matugen Dynamic Theming Engine. Kitty is the default terminal bound to SUPER + Return, and both terminals share the same typography, padding, opacity and palette.

docs.title: File Locations
docs.text:
• Repository source: ~/dotfiles/alacritty/alacritty.toml

  • Imported color palette: ~/.config/themes/current/alacritty.toml

docs.title: Dynamic Theme Integration (Matugen)
docs.text:
Alacritty delegates color palette definitions to an externally managed file generated by Matugen:

[general]
import = ["/home/zero/.config/themes/current/alacritty.toml"]
live_config_reload = true

docs.title: Live Update Workflow
docs.text:
1. Matugen processes the current desktop wallpaper or the manual theme selected via the Quickshell Control Center.
  2. It evaluates the template located at ~/.config/matugen/templates/alacritty.toml against the generated color roles.
  3. The resulting palette is written to ~/.config/themes/current/alacritty.toml.
  4. Because live_config_reload = true is enabled, all active Alacritty windows immediately update their colors without restarting or interrupting active shell sessions.

docs.title: Visual Settings & Typography
docs.text:
[window]
opacity = 0.92
padding = { x = 15, y = 15 }

[cursor]
style = { shape = "Underline", blinking = "On" }

[font]
normal = { family = "BlexMono Nerd Font", style = "Bold" }
bold   = { family = "BlexMono Nerd Font", style = "Bold" }
italic = { family = "BlexMono Nerd Font", style = "Bold Italic" }
  • Padding: Configured to 15 x 15 px to ensure clean breathing room between terminal text and Hyprland window borders.
  • Opacity: 0.92, providing subtle background transparency that blends with Hyprland dual-layer blur while maintaining high contrast and readability.
  • Font: BlexMono Nerd Font (Bold weight) for crisp glyph rendering and comprehensive icon support, matching Wofi Launcher.

docs.title: Associated Keybindings
docs.text:
• No default keybinding: SUPER + Return launches the default terminal (Kitty Terminal, see the Hyprland Keybindings Catalog).
  • Launch Alacritty from the Wofi Application Launcher or from scripts such as hypr/scripts/sudo-launcher.

docs.title: Kitty Configuration
docs.text: Kitty is the default terminal emulator in this environment, bound to SUPER + Return through the $terminal variable in Hyprland and running the Zsh Shell. Its configuration deliberately mirrors Alacritty: identical typography, padding, opacity and cursor behavior, with the color palette supplied by the Matugen Dynamic Theming Engine.

docs.title: File Locations
docs.text:

docs.title: Dynamic Theme Integration (Matugen)
docs.text:
Kitty does not define any static colors in its main configuration. It includes an externally generated palette file, keeping the same central-store architecture used by Alacritty:

include ~/.config/themes/current/kitty.conf

The palette template is adapted from the kitty template of matugen-themes (MIT license) and maps Material Design 3 color roles onto the complete terminal palette: the 16 ANSI colors, cursor and selection, URL color, tab bar, border colors, marks, and the extended 256-color range consumed by prompt themes such as Starship.

docs.title: Live Update Workflow
docs.text:
1. Matugen processes the current desktop wallpaper or the manual theme selected via the Quickshell Control Center.
  2. It evaluates the template located at ~/.config/matugen/templates/kitty.conf against the generated color roles.
  3. The resulting palette is written to ~/.config/themes/current/kitty.conf.
  4. The template's post_hook (pkill -SIGUSR1 kitty || true) signals every running kitty instance, which reloads the configuration in place without interrupting active shell sessions.

Unlike Alacritty, kitty does not watch included files on its own. The SIGUSR1 signal plays exactly the same role as Alacritty's live_config_reload = true. A manual reload is also available with Ctrl + Shift + F5.

docs.text:
window_padding_width 15
background_opacity 0.92

cursor_shape underline
cursor_blink_interval 0.5

font_family family="BlexMono Nerd Font" style="Bold"
bold_font family="BlexMono Nerd Font" style="Bold"
italic_font family="BlexMono Nerd Font" style="Bold Italic"

  • Padding: 15 px on every edge, matching the 15 x 15 padding used by Alacritty and keeping clean breathing room against Hyprland window borders.
  • Opacity: 0.92, identical to Alacritty, providing subtle background transparency that blends with Hyprland dual-layer blur while maintaining high contrast and readability.
  • Font: BlexMono Nerd Font with the Bold weight used as the normal style through the family= / style= font specification, replicating Alacritty's [font] block. font_size 11.0 keeps kitty visually aligned with Alacritty's default rendered size.
  • Cursor: underlined shape with a 0.5 s blink interval. shell_integration no-cursor prevents Zsh from overriding the cursor shape announced by shell integration.

docs.title: Vim Configuration
docs.text: Vim serves as the modal terminal text editor in this environment, configured with modern UI ergonomics, dynamic Material Design 3 theming generated by Matugen (with SynthWave '84 as fallback), vim-airline status bar theming, NERDTree file explorer, and full system clipboard synchronization under Debian and Wayland.

docs.title: File Structure & Paths
docs.text:
• Repository configuration: ~/dotfiles/vim/vimrc
  • Vim directory & plugins: ~/dotfiles/vim/dot-vim
  • Active user symlinks:
  • ~/.vimrc -> ~/dotfiles/vim/vimrc
  • ~/.vim -> ~/dotfiles/vim/dot-vim

docs.title: System Dependencies (Debian / Wayland)
docs.text:
To enable seamless copy/paste integration with Wayland and manage plugins, the following packages are required on Debian:

sudo apt install vim-gtk3 wl-clipboard
  • vim-gtk3: Replaces the default vim.basic binary with a version compiled with +clipboard and +xterm_clipboard. This activates set clipboard=unnamedplus in terminal sessions without launching a graphical window.
  • wl-clipboard: Provides wl-copy and wl-paste command-line tools for native clipboard buffer management in Wayland / Hyprland.
  • git & curl: Required by the vim-plug package manager to fetch and update plugin repositories.

docs.title: Plugin Architecture (vim-plug)
docs.text:
Plugins are managed via junegunn/vim-plug stored in ~/.vim/autoload/plug.vim and cloned into ~/.vim/plugged/:

  • preservim/nerdtree: Tree-style directory viewer and file explorer.
  • artanikin/vim-synthwave84: Neon synthwave color scheme kept as an automatic fallback when no Matugen palette has been generated yet.
  • vim-airline/vim-airline: Lightweight, customizable bottom statusline.
  • vim-airline/vim-airline-themes: Theme collection for vim-airline (configured to matugen, which mirrors the active colorscheme).

docs.title: Dynamic Matugen Theme
docs.text:
The active colorscheme follows the desktop palette generated by Matugen from the current wallpaper:

  • Colorscheme loader: ~/.vim/colors/matugen.vim sources the generated palette from ~/.config/themes/current/matugen.vim and silently falls back to synthwave84 if the file does not exist yet.
  • Airline loader: ~/.vim/autoload/airline/themes/matugen.vim exposes the same palette to vim-airline (normal, insert, visual, replace and inactive section colors). It only sources the generated file when the palette variable is not defined, so highlight groups are never cleared twice on startup.
  • Generation source: ~/dotfiles/matugen/templates/matugen.vim, wired through the [templates.vim] entry in ~/.config/matugen/config.toml.
  • Airline palette guard: the generated file builds the airline palette only when g:loaded_airline is set, because airline#themes#generate_color_map is an autoload function that cannot be detected with exists() before it has been loaded.

The repository vimrc rendered with the generated palette, including the synchronized vim-airline statusline:

docs.title: Theme refresh workflow
docs.text:
# Regenerate every palette (including matugen.vim) from the active wallpaper
bash ~/dotfiles/themes/apply-matugen.sh

Already running instances pick up the new palette with :colorscheme matugen, which reloads both the highlight groups and the airline palette in place.

docs.title: Zsh Shell Configuration
docs.text: Zsh serves as the interactive login shell across all terminal sessions (such as Alacritty), optimized for instant startup times, intelligent history handling, asynchronous-like autosuggestions, and streamlined Git integration within the Dotfiles Architecture.

docs.title: File Locations & Symlinks
docs.text:
• Configuration root: ~/dotfiles/zsh/zshrc -> ~/.zshrc
  • Aliases: ~/dotfiles/zsh/zshrc_aliases -> ~/.zshrc_aliases
  • Custom Prompts: ~/dotfiles/zsh/prompts/ -> ~/.zsh/prompts/
  • Plugin storage: ~/.zsh/plugins/ (managed via ~/dotfiles/install.sh, see Dotfiles Workflow)
  • Private overrides: ~/.zshrc_private (local machine only, unversioned)

docs.title: Startup Performance & Completion Cache
docs.text:
To eliminate the latency commonly associated with heavy frameworks like Oh-My-Zsh or Prezto, the configuration implements lightweight, native Zsh mechanisms with a 24-hour cache check on the completion dump:

autoload -Uz compinit
setopt extendedglob
if [[ -n ${ZDOTDIR:-$HOME}/.zcompdump(#qN.mh+24) ]]; then
    compinit
else
    compinit -C
fi
  • Cache check (#qN.mh+24): If the compiled completion dump (.zcompdump) was modified within the last 24 hours, compinit -C runs directly, bypassing expensive filesystem scans.
  • Measured startup time: ~120 ms for cold interactive start with all active plugins and completions loaded.

docs.title: Completion Menu & Visual Styling
docs.text:
The completion system is styled to match the dark terminal palette with interactive arrow navigation and detailed process inspection:

  • Tab menu navigation: zstyle ':completion:*' menu select=2 enables interactive visual grid selection upon pressing Tab.
  • Case-insensitive matching: Matches lowercase queries against uppercase files and handles dot/underscore boundaries automatically.
  • Process kill helper: Provides highlighted process listing (PID, %CPU, TTY, TIME, CMD) when running kill <Tab>.
  • Colorization: Synchronized with $LS_COLORS evaluated via dircolors -b.

docs.title: History Configuration & Privacy
docs.text:
HISTSIZE=20000
SAVEHIST=20000
HISTFILE=~/.zsh_history

setopt hist_ignore_all_dups     # Remove older duplicates if a new command is recorded
setopt hist_save_no_dups        # Never write consecutive duplicate entries
setopt hist_ignore_space        # Commands prefixed with leading whitespace are excluded from history
setopt hist_reduce_blanks       # Strip superfluous whitespace before writing
setopt share_history            # Interactively share history across concurrent terminal tabs
setopt inc_append_history       # Append history entries immediately upon command execution

The hist_ignore_space setting enables safe command execution containing tokens, passwords, or secrets by simply prepending a space to the command line.

docs.title: Lightweight Plugin Ecosystem
docs.text:
All plugins are cloned as shallow submodules under ~/.zsh/plugins/ during install.sh without external plugin managers:

  1. zsh-autosuggestions:
  2. Suggests commands as you type based on your shell history and completions.
  3. Keybinding: Ctrl + Space triggers autosuggest-accept.
  4. zsh-history-substring-search:
  5. Type any substring and cycle through previous matches using Up and Down arrow keys.
  6. zsh-syntax-highlighting:
  7. Provides real-time syntax validation (green for valid commands/paths, red for invalid commands).
  8. Loaded strictly as the final plugin to ensure accurate terminal tokenization.
  9. zsh-completions:
  10. Additional third-party completion definitions added to fpath prior to compinit.

docs.title: CLI Integrations
docs.text:
The shell dynamically verifies and activates installed modern CLI utilities:

  • fzf: Activated via eval "$(fzf --zsh)" providing fuzzy reverse search (Ctrl + R) and fuzzy path completion (Ctrl + T).
  • zoxide: Smart directory jumper activated via eval "$(zoxide init zsh)" using the z command.
  • uv: Ultrafast Python package and tool runner, configured with shell completions via eval "$(uv generate-shell-completion zsh)".
  • lsd: Modern ls alternative with icons, tree views, and color schemes aliased to ls, ll (lsd -la), and lt (lsd --tree).
  • batcat / bat: Syntax-highlighted pager replacement aliased to cat (see Bat Configuration).

docs.title: Custom Prompts
docs.text: Custom prompts reside in ~/dotfiles/zsh/prompts/ and are registered via Zsh's built-in promptinit system.

docs.title: 1. Minimal (prompt minimal) - Default
docs.text: A fast, single-line prompt featuring: * Compressed path notation (_shrink_path): Converts deep paths like ~/Workspace/personal/project into ~/W/p/project to preserve horizontal terminal width. * Git status (vcs_info): Displays branch name in red, with * for unstaged changes and + for staged changes. * Exit code indicator: Changes prompt symbol to green › on exit 0 and red › [code] on non-zero return codes. * Right prompt (RPROMPT): Displays current timestamp (HH:MM) in muted grey.

docs.title: 2. Macbar (prompt macbar) - Alternative
docs.text: A two-line aesthetic prompt: * Line 1: Full directory path with Git branch badge in brackets. * Line 2: Indented prompt symbol (λ), green on success and red on failure. * Right prompt: Git branch icon (󰊢) and timestamp.
